title: Implement root controller fencing and readiness
description:
## Outcome

Implement root-controller authority and readiness on the scoped-v2 substrate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The first pilot uses the frozen E01 controller policy: 30-second lease, 10-second renewal, and 5-second stop margin.
- [ ] Acquisition and renewal advance a monotonic root scope epoch; the scope epoch remains distinct from each E04 work-claim fence.
- [ ] Every controller mutation carries the current scope epoch and is rejected when stale.
- [ ] Readiness is derived only from admitted work, dependencies, revision, claim state, and terminal evidence.
- [ ] Restart rebuilds the same ready set without releasing work twice.
- [ ] Lease loss stops new admissions and effects before ownership is relinquished.
close_reason: Completed; PR #41

title: Implement deterministic root PlanRevision admission
description:
## Outcome

Implement the minimum deterministic root `PlanRevision` admission transaction.

## Context

`ravel-b8d.1` shipped the pure gate: `validate_proposal` turns a typed `PlanProposal` plus
caller-resolved facts into an `AdmissibleProposal` carrying canonical bytes and a content address
(`src/domain/proposal.rs`). Nothing consumes it yet, and nothing makes admission the *only* way work
appears — `DbHandle::admit_work` is `pub` today, so any caller can create schedulable work with no
plan, no basis, and no bounds.

This task closes that. It is also the landing site for `ravel-bms` (closed): revision, dependency,
and transition validation were deliberately excluded from the frozen v1 projection and belong here.

**A frozen v1 invariant has to be lifted first.** Four places currently reject a head or projection
row that carries an active plan digest, because v1 had no plan concept:

| Site | Current rule |
|---|---|
| `src/sync/head.rs:409` | `root_head_supported` returns `head.active_plan_digest().is_none()` |
| `src/sync/head.rs:176` | `ScopeHeadTransition::new` requires `candidate.active_plan_digest() == observed.head.active_plan_digest()` |
| `src/db/projections.rs:352` | `ScopeProjectionEvent::new` rejects `active_plan_digest.is_some()` |
| `src/db/projections.rs:146` | schema `CHECK (active_plan_digest IS NULL)` on `scopes` |

Admission is exactly the transition that changes the active plan, so all four must move from "never"
to "only through an admission event".

## Current State

Work is admitted today with no plan, no dependencies validated beyond self-reference, and no bounds:

```rust
// src/db/worker.rs:394-410 — the direct path this task must close
pub async fn admit_work(
    &self,
    scope: &ScopeIdentity,
    work: WorkRef,
    dependencies: Vec<WorkId>,
    scope_epoch: NonZeroU64,
) -> Result<(), ApplyError> {
```

Only tests call it outside `projections` (`src/db/worker.rs:776`,
`src/distributed/lifecycle.rs:557`), so narrowing its visibility has no production blast radius.

```rust
// src/db/projections.rs:462-476 — existing per-revision admission, already idempotent on the
// canonical dependency set, already epoch-fenced
pub(crate) fn admit_work(
    connection: &mut rusqlite::Connection,
    scope: &ScopeIdentity,
    work: &WorkRef,
    dependencies: &[WorkId],
    scope_epoch: NonZeroU64,
) -> Result<(), ApplyError> {
    if dependencies.iter().any(|dependency| dependency == work.id()) {
        return Err(ApplyError::Conflict);
    }
```

```sql
-- src/db/projections.rs:110-130 — readiness is already a query, so "only newly admitted,
-- dependency-ready work becomes schedulable" needs no new flag, only a correct writer
SELECT work_id, work_revision FROM admitted_work AS ready
 WHERE ready.scope_id = ?1
   AND ready.terminal_result_digest IS NULL
   AND (ready.claim_lease_until IS NULL OR ready.claim_lease_until <= ?2)
   AND ready.work_revision = (SELECT MAX(newer.work_revision) ...)
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM work_dependencies AS dependency ...)
```

```rust
// src/db/projections.rs:697-720 — the existing atomic, idempotent single-event apply this
// transaction must compose with, not duplicate
pub(crate) fn apply_scope_event(
    connection: &mut rusqlite::Connection,
    event: &ScopeProjectionEvent,
) -> Result<ApplyOutcome, ApplyError> {
    let transaction = connection.transaction()?;
```

```rust
// src/scope.rs:772-783 — the payload-type registry a new admission payload must join
pub(crate) fn payload_type_registered(payload_type: &str) -> bool {
    if payload_type == ROOT_GENESIS_PAYLOAD_TYPE {
        return true;
    }
```

## Desired State

One deterministic admission entry point. Everything below is the minimum that satisfies the five
acceptance criteria; anything not listed is out of scope.

### 1. A durable admission event

A new `plan_admitted` payload type joined to `payload_type_registered`, carrying the admitted
`plan_digest` and nothing that is not already addressed by it. Admission is ordered and replayable
because it is an event, exactly like root genesis; the plan bytes themselves are an immutable object
under `plan_key` (`src/scope.rs:569`), addressed by the digest the event names.

**The address is domain-separated.** `plan_digest` is `SHA-256("ravel.plan.proposal\0" || CBOR)`,
not `sha256(canonical_bytes)`, so the plan object cannot be published with
`publish_immutable(key, bytes, plan_digest)` — the store recomputes a plain SHA-256
(`src/storage/s3.rs:399`) and would report an integrity mismatch. Either publish under the plain
digest and keep `plan_digest` as the logical address, or prepend the domain at the verifier. Decide
this explicitly and write it down; `ravel-b8d.1` recorded the hazard but did not resolve it.

### 2. Lift the four no-active-plan rejections

Each becomes "an active plan digest is permitted, and only an admission event may change it":

- `root_head_supported` accepts a head with an active plan.
- `ScopeHeadTransition::new` permits `candidate.active_plan_digest() != observed.active_plan_digest()`
  **only** when the event's payload type is `plan_admitted`, and requires the candidate's digest to
  equal the one that event names. Every other payload type keeps the unchanged-plan rule.
- `ScopeProjectionEvent::new` accepts an active plan digest under the same condition.
- The schema `CHECK` on `scopes.active_plan_digest` becomes a digest-shape check, mirroring
  `tail_event_digest` (`src/db/projections.rs:148-151`).

### 3. Bounds and budget

No bounds or budget concept exists anywhere in the tree, so this is the one genuinely new model.
Minimum viable, root-only:

- **Target bounds** are per-work-revision limits the proposal declares — a finite attempt cap and a
  finite deadline. Admission rejects a missing or non-finite bound before mutation and records the
  bounds with the work row, so no later path invents one.
- **Reserved budget** is a per-scope monotonic reservation against a limit the proposal cites. The
  limit is fixed by the first admitted revision; a later revision must cite the identical limit or
  fail closed. Admission checks `already_reserved + this_revision <= limit` and records the
  reservation in the same transaction.

This deliberately does **not** parse the campaign config for a budget: `AdmittedCampaignConfig`
carries opaque caller-canonical bytes (`src/scope.rs:426`), and inventing a config schema is a
separate concern. Escrow is post-signal (`docs/mvp-evolution-approach.md:255`) because the MVP root
has no children. If the reviewers judge the cited-limit model wrong, the alternative is a limit set
once at genesis; record whichever is chosen and why.

### 4. One transaction

A single `projections` function, called through one `DbHandle` command, that in one SQLite
transaction:

1. Re-checks the objective, proposal basis, dependency graph, bounds, budget, and current plan
   revision. Basis checking is `validate_proposal` — do not reimplement it. The facts it needs are
   resolved *inside* this transaction, so the check and the write see one snapshot.
2. Records the plan row, the work rows, the dependency edges, the target bounds, and the budget
   reservation.
3. Advances `scopes.active_plan_digest` and applies the admission event.

**Dependency graph validation** adds what `admit_work` lacks: every edge names work admitted by this
revision or already admitted in this scope, and the edge set is acyclic. `admit_work` today rejects
only self-dependency (`src/db/projections.rs:471-475`), which is the degenerate cycle.

**Idempotency and fail-closed.** Repeating the same admission is a no-op that reports success, keyed
on the event's operation identity the way `apply_scope_event` already is
(`src/db/projections.rs:49-52` `OPERATION_CONFLICT_SQL`, `DUPLICATE_EXISTS_SQL`). Different bytes
under the same identity, or a proposal whose parent is not the scope's current active plan, is
`ApplyError::Conflict`.

### 5. Close the direct paths

`DbHandle::admit_work` becomes `pub(crate)` and the admission transaction becomes its only caller;
the two test call sites move to the admission entry point or stay in-crate. `record_terminal` and
`record_claim` become `pub(crate)` for the same reason — completion is provable only from a sealed
claim (`src/distributed/claims.rs`), never from a direct call. Nothing outside the crate can then
create work or mark it complete.

### Simplicity gate

- No new trait, no registry beyond the one `payload_type_registered` line, no config knob.
- One new `projections` function and one new `DbHandle` command, not a module.
- Reuse `apply_scope_event`, `admit_work`, `READY_WORK_SQL`, `validate_proposal`, `ScopeHead`,
  `ScopeHeadTransition`, and `ApplyError` unchanged wherever possible. New SQL only for the plan,
  bounds, and budget rows.
- Two new tables at most (`admitted_plans` carrying the reservation, and bounds columns on
  `admitted_work`). Prefer columns on existing tables over a new table when the lifetime matches.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `src/scope.rs` | `PLAN_ADMITTED_PAYLOAD_TYPE`, its typed payload + wire form, registry line | admission must be an ordered durable event |
| `src/db/projections.rs` | schema (plan/bounds/budget, relaxed `active_plan_digest` CHECK), the admission transaction, dependency-graph and budget SQL, `ScopeProjectionEvent` active-plan rule | one atomic write |
| `src/db/worker.rs` | one new command + method; narrow `admit_work`, `record_claim`, `record_terminal` to `pub(crate)` | single entry point, no direct path |
| `src/sync/head.rs` | `root_head_supported`, `ScopeHeadTransition::new` plan-change rule, module doc | a head may now carry an active plan |
| `src/sync/replay.rs` | carry the active plan through replay (`src/sync/replay.rs:228`) | a rebuilt projection must reach the same plan |
| `src/domain/proposal.rs` | only if validation needs a fact the current `ProposalFacts` cannot express | it was designed for this caller |
| `tests/wire.rs` | admission event fixture and canonical-bytes assertions | matches how root genesis is pinned |

### Patterns to Follow

- `apply_scope_event` (`src/db/projections.rs:697`) is the model for an atomic, idempotent,
  conflict-detecting projection write: read current state, prove the transition, write, commit.
- `admit_work` (`:462`) is the model for epoch fencing and canonical-set idempotency.
- `decode_root_event` / `root_event_from_wire` (`src/scope.rs:800-880`) is the model for a typed
  payload with exact-binding validation and a canonicality gate.
- `distributed::claims` is the model for a scoped durable record with a `record` discriminator.
- Error enums stay flat and per-concern with static `Display` text.

### Blast Radius

`root_head_supported` is called from `scope_controller::read_supported`
(`src/distributed/scope_controller.rs`) and `replay::prepare` (`src/sync/replay.rs:191`); both must
keep working for a scope that now has an active plan. Every existing test that asserts
`active_plan_digest() == None` still has to pass for a scope with no admitted plan.

## Testing Strategy

- **Criterion 1** — the transaction rejects, before any row is written, each of: wrong objective, a
  basis `validate_proposal` refuses, a dependency edge naming unknown work, a cyclic edge set, a
  missing or non-finite bound, a budget reservation over the limit, a cited limit that differs from
  the admitted one, and a parent plan that is not the scope's active plan. Each with its own error,
  and each proven not to have mutated by reading the projection afterwards.
- **Criterion 2** — after one successful admission, the plan row, every work row, every dependency
  edge, the bounds, the reservation, and `scopes.active_plan_digest` are all present; a forced
  failure at the last step leaves none of them.
- **Criterion 3** — repeating the identical admission returns success and changes nothing;
  different bytes under the same operation identity, and a stale parent plan, both return
  `Conflict`.
- **Criterion 4** — `ready_work` returns exactly the newly admitted revisions whose dependencies
  carry terminal evidence, and nothing that a prior revision had already claimed or completed.
- **Criterion 5** — a compile-level assertion that the direct paths are gone: `admit_work`,
  `record_claim`, and `record_terminal` are not reachable from outside the crate. Verified by their
  `pub(crate)` visibility plus a test that admission is the only writer of `admitted_work`.
- Replay: a projection rebuilt from durable history reaches the same active plan, work rows,
  dependencies, bounds, and reservation.

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|--------------|
| `ravel-b8d.1` | Validate typed proposal bases before admission | closed dependency; supplies `validate_proposal` (PR #45) |
| `ravel-bms` | Move v1-only checks to scoped-v2 admission | closed transfer record; revision/dependency/transition checks land here |
| `ravel-l7q.1` | Root controller fencing and readiness | closed; supplies `ControllerAuthority` and the epoch fence |
| `ravel-1l4.3` | Apply one event atomically and idempotently | closed; supplies `apply_scope_event` |
| `ravel-1l4.6` | Gate readiness and expose only the immediate ready-work query | closed; supplies `READY_WORK_SQL` |
| `ravel-a3j.3` | Bound projection writes and replay growth | closed; replay limits still apply |
| `ravel-yno` | Bind work and observations to the admitted revision | downstream; owns adding plan/fence columns to executable records, so do **not** add them here |
| `ravel-b8d.3` | Issue and reconcile scoped EffectGrants | downstream; binds the admitted plan digest |
| `ravel-e1n.1` | Define the minimum Change workflow projection | downstream |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One transaction validates the objective, proposal basis, dependency graph, bounds, budget, and current plan revision.
- [ ] It atomically records the new plan, work rows, dependencies, target bounds, and reserved budget.
- [ ] Repeating the same operation is idempotent; conflicting bytes or a stale base fail closed.
- [ ] Only newly admitted, dependency-ready work becomes schedulable.
- [ ] Direct workflow-owned work creation and completion transitions are impossible.
- [ ] The four frozen no-active-plan rejections are lifted to "only an admission event may change the active plan", and a scope with no admitted plan behaves exactly as before.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, and `cargo test --locked -- --ignored --test-threads=1` are clean.

## Design Notes

- Design-risk gate: waived. The mechanism is designed through the spec pipeline instead, which
  supplies the operational-envelope pass this task needs.
- **Open fork, resolve explicitly:** how the plan object is content-addressed in the store, given the
  domain-separated `plan_digest` is not the plain digest the store verifies. Publishing under the
  plain digest and keeping `plan_digest` logical is the smaller change; making the verifier
  domain-aware is the other option.
- **Open fork, resolve explicitly:** budget limit provenance — cited by each proposal and pinned by
  the first admission, versus set once at genesis. The first avoids a config schema; the second is
  harder to get wrong. Record the choice and its reason.
- `ravel-yno` owns binding work rows to plan digest and authority fence. Adding those columns here
  would duplicate its acceptance criteria.
- Carried over from `ravel-b8d.1` review: `AdmissibleProposal::canonical_bytes` has no length cap.
  The publish boundary in this task should cap it the way `AdmittedCampaignConfig::new` does
  (`src/scope.rs:436-451`), or state that the store's oversize guard owns the limit.

## Pointers

- `docs/mvp-evolution-approach.md:185-250` — the `PlanRevision` sketch and the full list of what admission validates.
- `docs/epics.md:198-235` — P3 acceptance criteria.
- `src/db/projections.rs:29-230` — every SQL constant and the schema this change extends.
- `src/sync/head.rs:1-13` — the epoch ordering rule an admission event must respect.
- PR #45 — `ravel-b8d.1`'s review ledger, including the deferred length cap and the address hazard.
notes:
`ravel-bms` is the closed transfer record: revision, dependency, and transition validation was intentionally excluded from frozen v1 and belongs here.
DESIGN DECISION (LLM-as-judge, openai.gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh, after two competing rust-design-review proposals). Verdict: DECIDED: A with amendments.

The spec pipeline returned a hard design gate with four blocking contract questions, so the escalation path ran: proposal A (first-admission-only) vs proposal B (supersession with specified conservative drain), then an independent judge that fact-checked both against source.

Q4 SUPERSESSION: out of scope. active_plan_digest may only move None -> Some via a plan_admitted event; Some -> Some is rejected. docs/mvp-outline.md:993-998 conditions supersession on drain rules for unclaimed work, live claims, unexpired grants, and in-flight operations. The judge found B did NOT close that gate: claims.rs:250-257 compares plan lineage only AFTER a claim is sealed (a live claim returns NotSealed first), so B could not establish live-claim applicability; and grant_fence plus record_grant already exist in the projection, so B's 'no grants exist, the rule is vacuous' was wrong. B also created a real duplicate-execution window, which B itself conceded.

Q4 also changes validate_proposal: it must now require BOTH parent_plan_digest == None and active_plan_digest == None. The gate should not advertise a transition the durable layer refuses. Re-enabling supersession is then deleting one predicate.

Q1 WORKSPEC: WorkSpec { work: WorkRef, instructions_digest: Digest, dependencies: Vec<WorkRef>, bounds: TargetBounds }. Dependencies are exact WorkRefs, not work ids: docs/mvp-outline.md:976-984 makes plan_digest and work_revision part of authoritative work identity, and READY_WORK_SQL's MAX(work_revision) resolution is replaced by exact-revision equality. New admitted_plans table with UNIQUE(scope_id) and CHECK(parent_plan_digest IS NULL), which makes a second plan unrepresentable in the schema rather than only in code. admitted_work gains plan_digest, instructions_digest, max_attempts, deadline_unix_ms. instructions_digest stays a binding only; the judge noted scope::artifact_key merely builds a key and storage::artifacts uses a different key space, so digest presence is not blob availability (ravel-6pv owns that proof).

Q2 BOUNDS: TargetBounds { max_attempts: NonZeroU64, deadline_unix_ms: NonZeroU64 }, both 1..=9_999_999_999_999_999. The judge REJECTED both proposals' invented 64-attempt ceiling: docs/mvp-outline.md:2233-2252 says the campaign supplies finite attempts and no other numeric defaults are invented here, so the only ceiling is storage representability. Deadline is absolute Unix-epoch ms on the clock base claim leases already use; the judge also rejected A's claim that an absolute deadline breaks replay equivalence, because readiness already takes a caller-supplied now_ms.

Q3 BUDGET: root_genesis is the sole budget-limit authority; WireRootGenesisPayload gains budget_limit_units after config_digest, projected into scopes.budget_limit_units. The judge rejected A's 'no limit is needed because the prior reservation is provably zero' as a blocker: a first reservation can still exceed campaign authority, and a proposal-declared ceiling is authority from nowhere. Config bytes cannot carry it because they have no durable home (only config_digest is published). This changes canonical genesis bytes, so tests/wire.rs constants and the wire fixtures are regenerated together, per docs/mvp-evolution-approach.md:181-183; the spec's 'do not modify tests/wire.rs' constraint is lifted as internally contradictory.

FORECLOSED, with owners: a new child bead under ravel-b8d must specify cancellation, applicability, live-claim drain, grant drain, in-flight reconciliation, budget release, and duplicate-execution policy before Some -> Some can ship, and it must land after ravel-yno and ravel-b8d.3. ravel-b8d.3 owns attempt counting and reservation consumption. ravel-6pv owns instructions-blob publication proof. ravel-yno owns trusted terminal-evidence intake; until it lands, dependency-bearing work stays blocked in production.
STATUS at handoff: design fully resolved and recorded above; implementation NOT started. Worktree ravel-wt/b8d.2 sits clean at db658bb (the b8d.1 tip) with all 115 tests green, so nothing is half-applied.

Why stopped rather than partially landed: the judge's amended contract makes this a multi-file durable-format change (7 source files plus regenerated wire fixtures), not the single additive module b8d.1 was. Landing it half-done would leave a broken tree and an unreviewable diff. The contract is the expensive part and it is now settled, so a resuming session starts from a fixed target.

RESUMPTION ORDER, each step ending green:
1. src/scope.rs: PLAN_ADMITTED_PAYLOAD_TYPE (added to payload_type_registered), PlanAdmittedPayload/PlanAdmittedEvent plus encode/decode through the existing encode_scope_event codec, budget_limit_units on RootGenesisPayload + WireRootGenesisPayload (appended after config_digest) + AdmittedCampaignConfig, and MAX_BUDGET_UNITS = 9_999_999_999_999_999. Then thread the new AdmittedCampaignConfig::new argument through its 13 call sites in 9 files.
2. tests/wire.rs and tests/fixtures/wire/: regenerate the genesis event fixture (its filename embeds the digest), root-head.json's tail_event_digest, and the EVENT_DIGEST / EVENT_BASENAME / include_bytes! / PAYLOAD_FIELDS constants. Per docs/mvp-evolution-approach.md:181-183 the contract and its fixtures change together.
3. src/domain/proposal.rs: WorkSpec, TargetBounds, their wire forms, work_specs + reserved_budget_units on PlanProposal, budget_limit_units on ProposalFacts, the first-admission-only predicate, and the canonical decode path with the 1 MiB cap plus digest verification and byte-equality re-encode. New ProposalError variants for duplicate work, unknown dependency, cycle, bound range, and budget.
4. src/db/projections.rs: the four schema changes, READY_WORK_SQL and RESUMABLE_WORK_SQL exact-revision rewrites, the admission transaction, the ScopeProjectionEvent active-plan rule, and TABLES / validate_text / validate_history / the query-plan test.
5. src/db/worker.rs: prepare_admission and apply_admission commands; remove DbHandle::admit_work and DbHandle::record_terminal and make the projection helpers private.

WATCH OUT: the repo's comment-steering hook rejects doc prose it judges an unsupported claim, a vague referent, or missing a why, and it evaluates line by line, so multi-line rationale sentences get flagged mid-sentence. Keep each new doc line short and self-contained, or append 'commentlint: allow(JUDGE)' where the claim is verified. The same hook gates commit messages.

Also note: this worktree's branch is task/ravel-b8d.2 but the session cwd is the main repo on main, so the main-branch guard sees main and blocks git commit. Assert the branch first, then commit with ALLOW_MAIN=1 from inside the worktree.
DESIGN DECISION SUPERSEDED. Second judge round (same model) after the user directed docs/mvp-evolution-approach.md as governing and simplest-correct-for-MVP as the bar. Lanes: ponytail-review (deletion) + rust-design-review correctness audit (wrong simplifications). Verdict: DECIDED: S2 with amendments. The judge OVERTURNED its own prior verdict.

DROPPED from the previous contract, each with the bead that owns it: genesis budget_limit_units and the 13-call-site plus wire-fixture churn (ravel-b8d.3 must establish a scope-derived ceiling before the first positive EffectGrant); the admitted_plans table (new supersession child bead); admitted_work.plan_digest and the active-plan query filter (ravel-yno); instructions_digest (ravel-e1n.1 for the WorkSpec instruction shape); the work_dependencies revision column, PK/FK changes, and exact-revision query rewrites (new supersession child bead, after ravel-yno); Some -> Some admission (same bead, after ravel-yno and ravel-b8d.3); attempt counting and reservation consumption (ravel-b8d.3).

WHY: under first-admission-only every work_id has exactly one revision, so the active-plan filter and exact-revision dependency resolution are predicates no reachable state can falsify. A predicate that cannot fire does not earn a schema change, and the exact-revision rewrite would have deleted two existing tests that encode the structural-invalidation semantics the future drain bead needs. Budget availability is scoped by docs/mvp-evolution-approach.md:249 to child proposals, which a root-only MVP cannot represent; the honest reading is :248 finite bounds, which representability validation delivers.

BLOCKER the earlier round missed, now fixed in scope: replay loses every admitted work row. src/sync/replay.rs:123-149 deletes and rebuilds the projection, src/sync/replay.rs:226-250 discards the payload and stamps head state, and src/domain/proposal.rs:328-332 says there is no decode path. After a rebuild the scope would come back with an active plan, zero schedulable work, and first-admission-only refusing re-admission forever, silently. Fix: a canonical plan decode path, and store the plan object as b"ravel.plan.proposal\0" || canonical_cbor under the existing plan_key. Because the stored bytes are then exactly the hash preimage, sha256(stored) equals plan_digest and publish_immutable verifies unchanged. That also dissolves the content-addressing fork at zero storage cost.

OTHER AMENDMENTS: objective_digest is written on genesis projection, never at admission, or AC1's objective check is a self-comparison. First-admission policy lives in the durable layer as a conditional UPDATE ... AND active_plan_digest IS NULL with rowcount 0 meaning Conflict, so validate_proposal's shipped parent == active rule stays unchanged and a later bead deletes one clause instead of re-widening a published gate. The row writer must take a &Transaction because both apply_scope_event and admit_work currently open their own, and AlreadyApplied must re-assert the rows rather than return early. RESUMABLE_WORK_SQL gains the deadline predicate too, or the bound stops new starts but not continuations. DbHandle::admit_work and DbHandle::record_terminal are deleted rather than narrowed, since pub(crate) fences nothing in a single-crate binary.

FACT CORRECTIONS the judge made against the lanes: the ponytail lane was wrong that the campaign config bytes could later be parsed for a ceiling, because src/scope.rs:624-640 hashes them and only config_digest is stored, and the sole production immutable-blob publisher is src/storage/artifacts.rs:66. The correctness lane was wrong that an inline 1 MiB plan payload fits, because src/scope.rs:29-30 caps the whole decompressed event at 1 MiB. Both lanes named ravel-6pv as a future owner, but it is closed and superseded.

AdmissibleProposal::canonical_bytes became stored_bytes and now carries the domain prefix, so plan_digest is the plain sha256 of the published object and publish_immutable verifies it unchanged. title: Issue and reconcile scoped EffectGrants
description:
## Outcome

Issue and reconcile scoped EffectGrant records separately from work claims.

## Context

`ravel-b8d.2` (PR #46) shipped admission: work rows exist only through an admitted plan, with
`max_attempts` and `deadline_unix_ms` bounds and a `scopes.reserved_budget_units` reservation
recorded but not yet consumed. `record_grant` already binds `admitted_work.grant_fence` to the
exact claim fence (`src/db/projections.rs:79-81`), and `distributed::claims` is the model for a
scoped durable record: JSON, 4 KiB cap, `record` discriminator, exact-binding decode, fail-closed
mismatch, deterministic key (`src/distributed/claims.rs`).

Two obligations carried from b8d.2 land here: a scope-derived budget ceiling before the first
positive grant (the plan's own `reserved_budget_units` is that ceiling), and attempt/consumption
accounting at grant issuance.

## Desired State (minimum)

One new module `src/distributed/grants.rs`, mirroring `claims.rs`:

- `EffectGrant` binds `ScopeClaimIdentity` (scope, plan digest, work revision, claim fence) plus
  `action`, `resource_scope`, `attempt`, `limit_units`, `deadline_unix_ms`, and `operation_id`
  (AC1). All key-segment validated; deadline and units NonZeroU64-bounded like `TargetBounds`.
- `scope_grant_key(scope, work, claim_fence)` in `src/scope.rs` beside `scope_claim_key`: one
  grant per claim generation, addressable without listing (AC4 reconciliation reads it back).
- Issuance is a function taking `&ControllerAuthority` (proof of current root controller) and the
  observed head's `active_plan_digest` (admitted plan) — AC2. It publishes the grant record with
  `put_if_absent` and reconciles an ambiguous outcome by reading the key back and comparing
  `operation_id` (AC4), the `claims.rs` intake idiom.
- Fail-closed use-side validation (AC3): `validate_grant(grant, expected: &ExpectedGrant, now_ms)`
  rejects expired (deadline <= now), stale fence (fence != expected), wrong revision/plan/scope,
  and wider-than-requested (units or deadline above the request). Revocation is representable as
  supersession: a grant for a superseded claim fence is stale by the fence rule.
- Grant limits draw on the plan reservation: issuance requires
  `limit_units + this scope's prior grant consumption <= reserved_budget_units`, accumulated in a
  new `admitted_work.granted_units` running total by the RECORD_GRANT_SQL conditional UPDATE, and
  `attempt <= max_attempts` from the admitted row. Rowcount 0 = Conflict. Re-recording the same
  grant object at the same fence draws nothing further, so issuance retry stays idempotent, and
  `admitted_work.grant_digest` is what makes that object identity checkable at intake.
- A grant grants execution only: no code path from a grant creates an `admitted_work` row or
  writes `terminal_result_digest` (AC5) — enforced structurally, as in b8d.2. `record_grant`
  updates the grant-accounting columns (`grant_fence`, `grant_digest`, `granted_attempt`,
  `granted_units`) on an existing row only.

## Out of scope (owners)
Delegation grants/escrow (post-signal); launcher enforcement at execution entry (ravel-1rc);
manifests (ravel-85q.2); plan/fence columns on executable records (ravel-yno).

## Acceptance criteria (verbatim)
- A grant binds scope, plan digest, work revision, claim fence, action, resource scope, limits, deadline, and operation identity.
- Grant issuance is authorized by the current root controller and admitted plan.
- Expired, revoked, stale-fence, wrong-revision, or wider-than-requested grants fail closed.
- Ambiguous issuance is reconciled by operation identity before retry.
- A grant cannot create work or prove completion.
- fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, ignored gates clean.

title: Own bounded intake, lifecycle, and shutdown
description:
## Outcome

Extend the completed E03 single-owner writer and E04 sealed-submission intake into one bounded root-node lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every internal queue has a fixed capacity and an explicit overload outcome.
- [ ] Sealed-submission validation preserves E04 identity, fence, revision, digest, and terminal-claim checks.
- [ ] Submission reads use configured bounded concurrency; a 32-item fixture records latency and proves concurrency never exceeds the cap.
- [ ] Cancellation, timeout, crash, and shutdown stop admission, reconcile unknown outcomes, kill descendants, drain durable writes, and then exit.
- [ ] Restart resumes only work whose scope epoch, revision, claim, and grant are still current.

title: Bound projection writes and replay growth
description:
## Outcome

Bound projection writes and prove replay has a scale-compatible growth curve.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The SQLite writer uses a bounded queue with explicit `full` and `stopping` outcomes.
- [ ] A stalled-writer stress test issuing 100,000 submissions shows resident memory reaches a stable bound.
- [ ] Replay benchmarks cover histories from 256 through 4,096 events.
- [ ] After warm-up, doubling history does not approach four times the replay time; any regression fails the benchmark gate.
- [ ] Batching or indexing changes preserve deterministic transaction and cursor semantics.
notes: Closed E03 remains valid. This task fixes the known extension risks: its local writer queue is unbounded and its history checks can approach quadratic replay as the chain grows.

title: Define scoped-v2 identity and the frozen-v1 boundary
description:
## Outcome

Define the scoped-v2 identity and wire boundary without changing frozen v1 bytes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] v2 durable identity includes `campaign_id`, `scope_id`, explicit `parent_scope_id` and `delegation_digest` slots, `plan_digest`, `work_id`, `work_revision`, claim fence, and scope epoch where applicable.
- [ ] The MVP accepts only a root scope with the canonical no-parent and no-delegation encoding; non-root values fail closed until recursive admission ships.
- [ ] Root scope genesis is deterministic from admitted campaign configuration.
- [ ] v2 envelopes and keys are distinct from v1.
- [ ] Mixed-version chains, unknown versions, and invalid identities fail before domain conversion.
- [ ] Frozen v1 fixtures still decode to the same bytes and meaning.

title: Implement the root-scope log, projection, and replay
description:
## Outcome

Implement the immutable root-scope log, `ScopeHead`, projection, and replay path by extending the completed E02 and E03 algorithms through separate v2 types.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Head, event, and claim keys are indexed by root `scope_id` and cannot collide with v1 keys.
- [ ] Every event binds its scope, sequence, parent, writer epoch, operation, payload type, and payload version.
- [ ] Conditional publication preserves E02's create, CAS, retained-chain, and unknown-outcome rules.
- [ ] Replay validates the complete retained chain before committing a disposable projection and preserves E03's atomic cursor semantics.
- [ ] Replaying the same chain is idempotent and produces the same projection.
- [ ] Artifact-bearing records are either projected by scoped-v2 or rejected before publication; frozen v1 behavior is unchanged.

title: Validate typed proposal bases before admission
description:
## Outcome

Validate typed proposal bases before root-plan admission.

## Context

Epic `ravel-b8d` makes an admitted root `PlanRevision` the only path that creates or
changes executable work. Admission (`ravel-b8d.2`) is one deterministic transaction; this
task ships the **pure gate that runs first**: the typed proposal record, its canonical
byte form, and the fail-closed basis validation. Nothing in `src/` models a plan proposal
today — `plan_digest` appears only as an opaque `Digest` carried by `ScopeHead`
(`src/scope.rs:365`), `ScopeClaimIdentity` (`src/scope.rs:153`), and `plan_key`
(`src/scope.rs:569`). There is no record of what a plan *contains* or what informed it, so
there is nothing to reject a stale, cross-scope, or unsupported basis with.

Splitting this from `ravel-b8d.2` keeps the transaction free of judgement: by the time the
admission transaction opens, the proposal is already a validated, content-addressed value.

## Current State

Only the opaque digest exists. There is no proposal, plan, or basis type:

```
$ grep -rn "PlanRevision\|proposal" src/
(no matches)
```

```rust
// src/scope.rs:363-372 — the head carries a plan digest but no plan content
pub struct ScopeHead {
    scope: ScopeIdentity,
    authority: ScopeAuthority,
    scope_epoch: NonZeroU64,
    tail: ScopeEventRef,
    active_plan_digest: Option<Digest>,
    operation_id: String,
}
```

```rust
// src/scope.rs:196-215 — the existing sequence+digest reference an observation basis would cite
pub struct ScopeEventRef {
    sequence: u64,
    digest: Digest,
}

impl ScopeEventRef {
    pub fn new(sequence: u64, digest: Digest) -> Result<Self, ValidationError> {
        validate_sequence(sequence)?;
        Ok(Self { sequence, digest })
    }
}
```

```rust
// src/db/projections.rs:472-478 — the repo's existing canonical-set idiom: sort then dedup
let mut dependencies = dependencies.iter().map(WorkId::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>();
dependencies.sort_unstable();
dependencies.dedup();
```

```rust
// src/scope.rs:634-648 — the repo's existing domain-separated digest derivation
pub fn root_scope_id(workspace: &WorkspaceId, campaign: &CampaignId) -> Result<ScopeId, WireError> {
    let seed = RootScopeSeed { workspace_id: workspace.as_str(), campaign_id: campaign.as_str() };
    let mut cbor = Vec::new();
    into_writer(&seed, &mut cbor).map_err(|_| WireError::InvalidEncoding)?;
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(ROOT_SCOPE_DOMAIN);
    hasher.update(&cbor);
    ScopeId::new(format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize())).map_err(|_| WireError::InvalidValue)
}
```

## Desired State

One new module, `src/domain/proposal.rs`, holding a validated proposal value plus a pure
validation function. No trait, no registry, no config knob.

**Header bindings (acceptance criterion 1).** A proposal cites, in its own bytes:
`scope_id`, `objective_digest`, `parent_plan_digest: Option<Digest>`, and its typed basis
list. The header carries the mandatory bindings; the list carries the variable ones.

**Typed basis (criterion 1).** `ProposalBasis` has exactly two variants for the root-only
MVP — `Observation { event: ScopeEventRef }` and `PriorRevision { plan_digest: Digest }`.
Child certificates and delegation bases are post-signal (`docs/epics.md:227`) and are not
modelled. An untyped or free-form basis is unrepresentable.

**Canonical ordering (criterion 4).** Construction sorts the basis list into one total
order (observations before prior revisions; observations by `(sequence, digest)`; prior
revisions by digest) and dedups it, mirroring `admit_work`'s sort-then-dedup idiom. The
`plan_digest` is SHA-256 over a domain-separated CBOR encoding of the ordered proposal, so
two callers that supply the same set in different order and with duplicates derive
byte-identical bytes and one digest.

**Fail-closed validation (criteria 2 and 3).** `validate_proposal(&PlanProposal, &ProposalFacts)`
is pure and returns `Result<AdmissibleProposal, ProposalError>`. `ProposalFacts` carries
what the caller resolved from durable state: the scope identity, the admitted
`objective_digest`, the scope's current `active_plan_digest`, the projected tail sequence,
and the resolved facts for each cited observation (`scope_id`, `ScopeEventRef`,
`payload_type`). Every rejection is a distinct `ProposalError` variant and happens before
any mutation, because the function performs no I/O at all:

| Rejection | Rule |
|---|---|
| cross-scope | a cited observation's `scope_id` differs from the header's |
| missing | a cited observation has no resolved fact, or its sequence exceeds the projected tail |
| stale | a resolved fact's digest differs at that sequence; `parent_plan_digest` differs from `active_plan_digest`; a `PriorRevision` names anything other than `active_plan_digest` |
| unsupported | a resolved fact's `payload_type` is not a planning input |
| cyclic | a `PriorRevision` names this proposal's own `plan_digest` |
| objective mismatch | header `objective_digest` differs from the admitted one |

**Planning-input allow-list.** A `const` slice, initially `["root_genesis"]` — the root
genesis event is the durable objective/configuration record (`src/scope.rs:299-307`). No
observation payload type exists in the codebase yet, so anything else fails closed until
its payload type ships, exactly like `payload_type_registered` (`src/scope.rs:772`).

**Simplicity gate.** `ProposalFacts` is a plain borrowed struct, not a trait: there is one
caller (`ravel-b8d.2`'s transaction) and one test caller. Facts are resolved by the caller
so this module stays pure and exhaustively testable without SQLite. The projection query
that supplies them belongs to `ravel-b8d.2`, whose acceptance criterion already covers
"one transaction validates the objective, proposal basis, ...".

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `src/domain/proposal.rs` | new module: `ProposalBasis`, `PlanProposal`, `ProposalFacts`, `ObservationFact`, `AdmissibleProposal`, `ProposalError`, `validate_proposal` | the whole task; one file keeps the gate reviewable |
| `src/lib.rs` | add `pub mod proposal;` under `pub mod domain` | module registration (`src/lib.rs:15-19`) |

Nothing else changes. No schema change: the facts a caller resolves come from columns
`applied_scope_events` already has (`scope_id`, `sequence`, `digest`, `payload_type`,
`src/db/projections.rs:154-160`).

### Existing Code to Reuse

A duplication check ran on "typed reference to a prior event or plan revision that
informed a proposal, canonically ordered so equivalent input hashes identically" before
this task was enriched. **Outcome: novel record, reuse every primitive.** No proposal or
plan-content type exists; every building block does:

- `src/scope.rs:78-96` — `Digest`: the validated 64-hex digest. Do not add a second digest newtype.
- `src/scope.rs:196-215` — `ScopeEventRef`: the exact `(sequence, digest)` pair an observation basis cites.
- `src/scope.rs:99-146` — `ScopeIdentity` / `ScopeId`: scope binding and the cross-scope comparison.
- `src/scope.rs:634-648` — `root_scope_id`: the domain-separated `SHA-256(domain || CBOR(seed))` idiom to mirror for `plan_digest`.
- `src/db/projections.rs:472-478` — the sort-then-dedup canonical-set idiom.
- `src/domain/validation.rs:14-38` — `ValidationError`: extend only if a new category is genuinely needed; prefer a task-local `ProposalError`, matching how `claims.rs` and `sync` keep their own error enums.
- `src/domain/artifact.rs` — the shape to mirror for a validate-on-construction domain record with getters and no setters.

The implementing agent must read these locations and confirm the verdict still holds at
HEAD before writing new code.

### Patterns to Follow

- Validate on construction, expose getters only, keep fields private (`src/domain/artifact.rs:20-48`).
- One flat error enum per concern with `Display` + `Error` impls (`src/domain/validation.rs:14-38`, `src/sync.rs:8-27`).
- `deny_unknown_fields` + declaration-order serde structs for any wire form (`src/scope.rs:700-706`).
- Doc comments state the invariant and the exact rejection categories under `# Errors`.
- Tests are a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in the same file, table-driven over rejection cases (`src/domain/artifact.rs:76-134`).

### Blast Radius

None at HEAD: the module is additive and every item is `pub`, so no dead-code lint fires
while `ravel-b8d.2` is the only future caller. `ravel-b8d.2` consumes
`validate_proposal`; `ravel-b8d.3` consumes the validated `plan_digest` as the grant's plan
binding; `ravel-yno` binds work and observations to the admitted revision.

## Testing Strategy

Unit tests in `src/domain/proposal.rs`, one per acceptance criterion:

1. **Criterion 1** — a proposal round-trips its header bindings and typed basis list; a basis cannot be constructed without a typed reference.
2. **Criterion 2** — a cited observation with a resolved fact whose `payload_type` is a planning input validates; a fact from another `scope_id` and a fact with a non-planning `payload_type` each fail with their own variant.
3. **Criterion 3** — table-driven: missing fact, sequence past the tail, digest mismatch at the cited sequence, stale `parent_plan_digest`, `PriorRevision` naming a non-active digest, `PriorRevision` naming the proposal's own digest, and objective mismatch each return the named `ProposalError`. Validation performs no I/O, which is what "before mutation" means here.
4. **Criterion 4** — the same basis multiset supplied in several permutations, with duplicates, produces one identical byte string and one identical `plan_digest`; changing any single header binding changes the digest.

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|--------------|
| `ravel-b8d` | Phase 3: Root PlanRevision admission and effect authority | parent epic |
| `ravel-a3j.2` | Implement the root-scope log, projection, and replay | closed dependency; supplies `applied_scope_events` |
| `ravel-b8d.2` | Implement deterministic root PlanRevision admission | this task blocks it; it resolves the facts and runs the transaction |
| `ravel-b8d.3` | Issue and reconcile scoped EffectGrants | downstream; binds the admitted `plan_digest` |
| `ravel-yno` | Bind work and observations to the admitted revision | downstream |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every proposal cites the exact objective, plan digest, scope, and observation or prior revision it uses — as typed, private, validate-on-construction fields.
- [ ] Referenced observations exist, belong to the same root scope, and are allowed as planning input.
- [ ] Missing, stale, cross-scope, cyclic, or unsupported bases fail before mutation, each with its own `ProposalError` variant.
- [ ] Canonical ordering makes equivalent proposal inputs produce identical admitted bytes and one `plan_digest`.
- [ ] No new digest, identity, or event-reference newtype — `Digest`, `ScopeId`, and `ScopeEventRef` are the source of truth.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked` are clean.

## Design Notes

- Design-risk gate: waived. This task designs a *contract* (a validated record and a pure
  predicate), not a mechanism on an operational surface — no queue, lock, eviction policy,
  or sweep. The admission transaction's operational envelope belongs to `ravel-b8d.2`.
- Facts-in, not I/O-in: passing resolved facts keeps this module pure and lets every
  rejection be a cheap unit test. The alternative — a trait the projection implements —
  buys nothing at one implementation and costs a dyn/generic boundary.
- Two basis variants only. Certificates, delegation grants, and configuration bases are
  post-signal per `docs/epics.md:227`; adding variants now would be unreachable code.

## Pointers

- `docs/mvp-evolution-approach.md:185-250` — the `PlanRevision` sketch and the list of what admission validates.
- `docs/epics.md:198-235` — P3 acceptance criteria, including the immutability and typed-basis requirement.
- `src/scope.rs` — every primitive this module composes, and the canonical-bytes conventions.
- `src/distributed/claims.rs:380-560` — the closest existing sibling: a scoped record with canonical bytes, exact-binding decode, and fail-closed mismatch handling.
notes:
Review ledger (2 waves + sign-off, all lanes read their SKILL.md and the cumulative diff):
- rust-code-reviewer: 9 findings, no BLOCKING. Applied: fact-lookup precondition doc, rustdoc private-link fix, non-plain-sha256 + ciborium-pin note, PriorRevision-is-address-affecting note, AdmissibleProposal::scope_id, check-precedence doc, empty-basis doc, ProposalFacts derives, two untested normalization branches.
- less-code: deleted one subsumed happy-path test, folded a straggler assertion, removed duplicated prose and one vacuous assertion.
- reduce-complexity: no ACCIDENTAL hotspot; renamed the oversized test to what it covers, bound scope_id once, narrowed the module doc's reachability claim.
- invariant-test-review: ran a real mutation campaign (12 mutants). 8 survived. Fixed all: pinned GENESIS_PLAN_DIGEST (kills dropped-domain-prefix, wire-field rename, field-order swap), projected-tail guard case with a valid fact above the tail, third illegal parent/active combination, empty-basis path, sequence-over-digest tiebreak, prior-revision ordering.
- ponytail-review: ~50 net lines removed across prose and two subsumed table rows; module doc and # Errors compressed.
- doc-rigor: found one FALSE claim - the comment said an internally tagged serde enum buffers through serde::Content, which is untrue for struct variants (only newtype variants do). Replaced with the byte-level reason. Also corrected 'every field is a validated domain value' (payload_type is not), named objective_digest's real source (root-genesis config_digest; no projection table or head field carries it), and qualified the payload_type_registered analogy (its allow-list also admits test_successor under cfg(test)).
- Sign-off (round 1 of 2): rust-code-reviewer CLEAN, ponytail-review CLEAN. The reviewer independently recomputed the pinned plan digest from first principles and got the identical value.

Deferred to b8d.2/b8d.3: canonical_bytes carries no length cap here; the publish boundary should cap it the way AdmittedCampaignConfig::new does, or state that the store guard owns the limit.

title: Require claim and EffectGrant at every execution entry
description:
## Outcome

Require both current work ownership and explicit effect authority at every external execution entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entry verifies root scope, plan digest, work revision, scope epoch, claim fence, and `EffectGrant` subject.
- [ ] Claim ownership alone cannot authorize a model, sandbox, Git, S3, or code-host effect.
- [ ] A grant alone cannot bypass readiness or claim ownership.
- [ ] Stale, expired, revoked, mismatched, or replayed authority is rejected before the effect starts.
- [ ] The decision and rejection reason are recorded without secrets.
notes: Extends the closed E04 execution gate (`ravel-fn1` and `ravel-vsg.2`) by requiring separate effect authority. Existing `ClaimAuthority` remains necessary but is never sufficient for an external effect.

title: Phase 1: Root scoped-v2 substrate
description:
## Outcome

Add the root-only scoped-v2 substrate used by the MVP. Frozen v1 records remain valid and are never reinterpreted.

## Scope

- Versioned root scope identity and deterministic genesis.
- Scope-indexed immutable log, head, projection, and replay.
- Bounded local projection writes and replay that does not grow quadratically.

Child scopes and cross-scope recovery are post-signal work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A root scope can bootstrap, advance, restart, and rebuild deterministically.
- [ ] v1 and v2 records cannot appear in one authoritative chain.
- [ ] Unknown versions and malformed identities fail closed.
- [ ] Queue and replay bounds are measured and enforced.
notes:
Root-only MVP. Recursive child scopes are tracked under ravel-rec.
Completed inputs: E02's S3/CAS/retained-chain algorithms and E03's atomic projection/replay model. Implement them through separate scoped-v2 keys and types; do not reinterpret v1.

Pending merge evidence:

title: Phase 3: Root PlanRevision admission and effect authority
description:
## Outcome

Make a root-scope `PlanRevision` the only path that creates or changes executable work.

## Scope

The MVP admits one root plan at a time. Admission validates proposal bases, writes work and dependencies atomically, reserves bounds, and issues separate effect authority.

Delegation, escrow, completion certificates, settlement, and quarantine are post-signal work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No workflow or worker can create work or mark completion through a direct state transition.
- [ ] Admission is deterministic, atomic, idempotent, and revision-bound.
- [ ] Claim ownership and effect authority remain separate.
notes: Completed inputs: E03 atomic projection/readiness and E04 claim fences. `PlanRevision` admission and `EffectGrant` authority are new v2 records; they are not inferred from v1 rows.

title: Phase 2: Root authority and bounded lifecycle
description:
## Outcome

Provide root-scope controller authority and bounded node lifecycle for the MVP.

## Scope

One root controller owns admission and scheduling. Two workers may execute admitted work. Every loop has a queue bound, deadline, cancellation path, and restart rule.

Child-scope authority and settlement pressure are post-signal work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Stale controllers and workers cannot commit after an authority change.
- [ ] Restart reconstructs readiness from durable scoped state.
- [ ] Intake, execution, projection, and shutdown remain bounded.
notes: Completed inputs: E01's 30/10/5 controller policy, E03 readiness and single-writer rules, and E04 claim/submission fencing. Root `scope_epoch` and work `claim_fence` remain separate.
close_reason: Completed: PR #41 (ravel-l7q.1) fences root controller authority and derives readiness; PR #42 (ravel-l7q.2) bounds intake, submission validation, and shutdown. Epic criteria evidenced by tests listed in both PR bodies. Work-row admission payload remains ravel-b8d.2.

title: Cut the MVP to one product-validation slice
description:
## Outcome

Cut the MVP task graph to one product-validation path without removing the protocol seams needed for later scale.

## MVP path

Objective and bounds -> root scoped-v2 `PlanRevision` -> deterministic admission -> two workers -> claim plus `EffectGrant` -> one model provider -> Linux sandbox -> trusted local evaluation -> reviewable Change result -> user decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Active tasks form one complete Change campaign and product trial.
- [x] Root scope identity, versioning, authority, recovery, and bounded-resource seams remain explicit.
- [x] Recursive scopes, Research, code-host automation, and full scale/fault proofs are deferred with clear unlock conditions.
- [x] Superseded tasks and dependencies are closed or rewired.
- [x] `bd ready`, dependency-cycle checks, stale-reference checks, and JSONL validation pass.
- [x] The pull request changes Beads task data only.
close_reason: The MVP graph now has one Change product-validation path, explicit scale-safe seams, and deferred post-signal expansions. Validation passes and the PR contains task data only.

title: Bind work and observations to the admitted revision
description:
## Outcome

Bind every `WorkRef`, action, observation, and candidate to the admitted plan revision that produced it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `WorkRef` values can be constructed only from admitted work rows.
- [ ] Projections store scope, plan digest, work revision, and authority fence for executable records.
- [ ] Observations and actions retain the proposal basis and effect-grant attribution used to produce them.
- [ ] Stale-revision results remain auditable but cannot satisfy the current revision.
design:
ravel-yno plan v2 (forged: plan-forge round 1 dual review -> FORGE AGAIN, then 3-judge panels ruled all three design questions). Full plan at ~/.claude/plans/2026-08-16-ravel-yno-admitted-revision-binding-v2.md; v1 kept for diff.

Rulings that bind the work (bd memories): e06-admitted-work-witness (seal WorkRef itself; NO AdmittedWork witness type), e06-observation-attribution (defer the observation/action record, land the contract; no schema change), e06-stale-revision-proof (extend the existing supersession test; no new test).

AC verdicts: AC1 newly enforced by U1. AC2 already held by admitted_work columns, newly pinned by U2. AC3 partially met by design -- structurally reachable today via plan_digest -> PlanProposal::bases and grant_digest -> the grant, record shape deferred to ravel-85q.2, attribution constraint pinned by U3. AC4 already held by CLAIMABLE_WORK_SQL's active-plan arm and exact-revision dependency probe plus a_dependency_edge_is_satisfied_only_at_its_bound_revision; only the auditable half was unpinned, which U2 fixes.

U1 -- Seal WorkRef and remove the wire mint (AC1). src/domain/work.rs: WorkRef::new becomes pub(crate), name stays mechanism-honest (new, not from_admitted_row) because ~20 in-crate test sites fabricate references through it; the production invariant goes in the doc comment. src/scope.rs: GrantActivatedPayload holds work_id: WorkId plus a revision integer instead of a WorkRef, keeping the existing zero/MAX_STORED_INTEGER bound check at :410, with accessors work_id() and work_revision(); grant_activated_from_decoded at :1114 can then no longer mint a WorkRef from untrusted bytes; encode path at :1080-1081 reads the new accessors; scope_claim_key and scope_grant_key narrow to pub(crate). src/db/projections.rs fold binding at :1409-1410 reads the new accessors. src/distributed/grants.rs :345-346 passes grant.identity.work().id().clone() and .revision(). In-crate GrantActivatedPayload test constructions: src/scope.rs:1525,1602,1614,1619 and src/db/projections.rs:2677,2737,2854. tests/wire.rs: relocate scope_keys_cover_the_exact_identity_axis (197-247, including the zero-fence rejection at 242) into src/scope.rs's mod tests with expected key strings verbatim. Unchanged on purpose: WireGrantActivatedPayload (already flat, so no wire byte moves), decode_grant and decode_bound keep expected_work: &WorkRef from their row-reading caller and must not construct one, ScopeClaimIdentity::new keeps its signature.

U2 -- Pin the auditable half of AC4 and AC2's four bindings. Extend plan_supersession_withdraws_scheduling_and_keeps_the_superseded_row (src/db/projections.rs:3137) with one assertion that admitted_work_refs still returns the superseded (work-a, 1) row paired with ADMITTING_PLAN_DIGEST after the active plan moves to DIGEST_3. Every existing assertion on that row goes through a direct-SQL helper, so no public reader covered it. Together with the test's existing continuable(...) == ["work-a@1#2"] assertion (work id @ revision # claim fence) and the scope-scoped query, all four AC2 bindings are then asserted through public readers in one test, so AC2 needs no new test.

U3 -- Pin effect-grant attribution (AC3). One test that the applied_scope_events CHECK ((payload_type = 'grant_activated') = (grant_digest IS NOT NULL)) at :311 refuses both directions. validate_schema at :1645 compares a live file's DDL against the SCHEMA constant, so it catches file-versus-constant drift but not an edit to the constant, leaving the constraint's effect unguarded. Both violations are unreachable through apply_scope_event_in_transaction, so the test inserts directly, as this file already does for states production cannot produce.

U4 -- Contract already recorded in e06-observation-attribution; no source change. PR must state AC3 partially met and name ravel-85q.2.

Non-goals: supersession through the production path or its drain rules (testing the query rules IS in scope -- the repo already ships a supersede_plan helper and the panel drew that line explicitly); a new observation/action payload type; any change to payload_type_registered(), the SQL schema, SCHEMA_VERSION, frozen v1 conversion, or tests/fixtures bytes; token/model budget substrate; an AdmittedWork witness type.

Gates: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked. Skip --ignored (live S3 creds) and the x86_64 cross-check (host is aarch64; CI covers).

stage=plan (plan-forge round 1 dual review in flight). Plan v1 at ~/.claude/plans/2026-08-16-ravel-yno-admitted-revision-binding-v1.md. Substrate findings: WorkRef has a public infallible new() and is only constructed in 3 production sites (admit_plan from AdmissibleProposal specs, the projection row readers, and grant_activated_from_decoded from untrusted wire bytes); everything else is test fixtures. admitted_work already stores scope_id/work_id/work_revision/plan_digest/admitted_scope_epoch/claim_fence/grant_fence so AC2 is held but pinned by no test. No observation or action record exists anywhere (proposal.rs module doc says so), so AC3 has no substrate. admit_plan handles first admission only and no supersession bead exists, so AC4's stale-revision state is unreachable through the production path. Three design questions raised for routing: e06-admitted-work-witness (seal WorkRef itself vs add an AdmittedWork witness in db::projections following the PublishedArtifact precedent), e06-observation-attribution (defer the observation/action record and pin today's applied_scope_events.grant_digest biconditional vs widen the schema now vs mint a payload type that forks ravel-85q.2's canonical artifact-reference contract), e06-stale-revision-proof (prove the query rules against directly inserted two-plan rows vs enable supersession here vs defer AC4).

Four of the RETHINK findings existed only because v1 recommended an AdmittedWork witness type, and the DQ1 panel unanimously overturned that recommendation, so they dissolved rather than being patched; R1.C.F4 (wire decode mints a WorkRef from untrusted bytes at src/scope.rs:1114) became the core of U1 via the reviewer's own proposed option. Production WorkRef::new sites verified to be exactly src/db/projections.rs:829,834 (admission insert) and :1111,:1153,:1184 (row readers); tests/ references none of WorkRef, ScopeClaimIdentity, scope_claim_key, scope_grant_key.

Round 1: five parallel reviewers. less-code 0 findings. reduce-complexity 1 non-blocking. test-strategy 2 blocking. invariant-test-review 3 (1 blocking, 2 non-blocking). rust-code-reviewer 2 non-blocking. Blocking, all fixed: (a) the decoder is now the only place an activation payload's work identity is validated and no test exercised it there -- added repack-and-rekey cases so decode_grant_activated_event refuses an empty, slash-bearing, and 129-byte work_id plus revision 0 and MAX_STORED_INTEGER+1; (b) nothing pinned the stored address of an activation event, so a matched pair of encode/decode edits could move every event's digest, key and re-encode check undetected -- pinned via ACTIVATION_EVENT_DIGEST. title: Freeze downstream E05/E07/E09 contracts and treatment-neutral capture (E01 amendment)
description:
## Context

Plan-review reconciliation found that E05, E07, and E09 tasks assume contracts E01 must supply, but Tasks 1–4 closed without freezing all of them. Per the closed ravel-q3w.4 amendment rule, changes to `pilot/e01/` require a new Git revision and content digest before affected runs; this task is that amendment.

This task freezes the remaining downstream contracts and the treatment-neutral measurement capture needed for A/B/C comparability, before any prerequisite epic implements against assumptions.

## Desired State

`pilot/e01/` artifacts (extending `experiments.md` or small sibling files) freeze, to the extent Tasks 1–3 have not already frozen them:

- controller lease duration, renewal cadence, and stop margin;
- the one selected Linux containment mechanism with its mounts/limits/descriptors and the authoritative descendant-quiescence rule;
- path-component grammar, invalid-UTF-8 rule, Unicode normalization version, case/collision-key algorithm, and golden vectors;
- stable target identity, total order, tie behavior, deterministic packing rule, and positive group cap;
- treatment-neutral measurement capture: common run/attempt validity and invalid-attempt replacement rules; timing boundaries and fault placement; run-start and run-terminal records; per-host monotonic busy intervals; work-ready, dispatch, and terminal events; provider usage and cost; final-rediscovery completion; and reserved treatment-C run IDs for qualifying `ravel-85q.8` and `ravel-e1n.7` proofs, each counted as a C observation exactly once.

A new Git revision and content digest are recorded for the amended `pilot/e01/` set; old and amended results are not silently pooled.

## Implementation Guidance

- First audit the closed Tasks 1–3 artifacts (`environment.yaml`, `research.md`, the Task 3 Change contract) and the PR #6 `budgets.yaml`/`experiments.md`; freeze only what is genuinely missing. Do not restate already-frozen values.
- Follow the existing private `pilot/e01/` convention: flat scalars, fixed tables, golden vectors. No schema, validator, framework, or runtime module.
- The capture contract must be treatment-neutral: identical record shapes for A, B, and C so no treatment gains measurement advantage.
- Reserved C run IDs let one qualifying `ravel-85q.8` run and one qualifying `ravel-e1n.7` run count as treatment-C observations exactly once, only when executed under this frozen capture contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controller lease duration/renewal cadence/stop margin, the selected Linux containment mechanism and authoritative quiescence rule, path grammar/invalid-UTF-8/normalization/collision rules with golden vectors, and stable target identity/order/tie/packing/group-cap rules are frozen in `pilot/e01/` or verified already frozen, with exact locations cited. **(E05/E07/E10 contract dependencies)**
- [ ] Treatment-neutral capture is frozen: run/attempt validity and invalid-attempt replacement, timing boundaries and fault placement, run-start/terminal records, per-host monotonic busy intervals, work-ready/dispatch/terminal events, provider usage/cost, final-rediscovery completion, and reserved C run IDs for qualifying `ravel-85q.8`/`ravel-e1n.7` runs counted exactly once. **(E01 AC6)**
- [ ] A clean-checkout smoke regenerates and revalidates inventory, fixtures, path/collision golden vectors, containment preflight, orthogonal audit, and experiment capture fields; the new Git revision and content digest are recorded outside the hashed directory. **(E01 AC8)**
- [ ] The diff contains only private `pilot/e01/` artifacts; no framework, validator, or runtime module is added. **(E01 AC8)**

## Testing Strategy

- **Manual review:** table/vector review against the E05/E07/E09 task texts that consume each contract.
- **Live integration:** clean-checkout regeneration smoke and digest reproduction as above.

## Design Gate

Amendment authorized by plan-review reconciliation (Findings 6, 9); mechanism per closed ravel-q3w.4 amendment rule. No separate design review required.

## Final Step

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.

title: Run hidden deterministic local evaluation
description:
## Outcome

Execute hidden deterministic evaluation without exposing evaluator trust roots.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Evaluator code and hidden inputs remain outside candidate-visible mounts, file descriptors, process views, environment, and diagnostics.
- [ ] Candidate-controlled compilation and execution use the selected bounded sandbox with no shared writable cache.
- [ ] Each run produces immutable `PASS`, `FAIL`, `ERROR`, or `TIMEOUT` evidence.
- [ ] Evidence binds candidate, evaluator generation, policy, plan/work revision, claim, grant, and attempt.
- [ ] Canaries cover hidden-file, environment, descriptor, process, socket, network, and output-exfiltration paths.

title: Admit evidence and derive the mechanical gate
description:
## Outcome

Admit exact immutable evidence and derive one deterministic mechanical gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Evidence is accepted only for the exact current candidate, action, evaluator generation, policy, authority, and attempt.
- [ ] Required evidence is reduced by stable identity and precedence, independent of arrival order.
- [ ] `FAIL`, `ERROR`, and `TIMEOUT` cannot be hidden by another attempt's `PASS` unless the admitted retry policy explicitly supersedes it.
- [ ] Missing or conflicting evidence yields a non-passing state.
- [ ] The reducer is replay-deterministic.

title: Define trusted evaluator generation and routing
description:
## Outcome

Define trusted evaluator generations and exact routing for the selected Change pilot.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trusted configuration maps each admitted evaluation action to one evaluator generation and policy digest.
- [ ] Candidate code cannot select commands, hidden inputs, trust roots, or pass criteria.
- [ ] Unsupported action, candidate, generation, or policy combinations fail closed.
- [ ] Routing binds scope, plan revision, work revision, candidate, and attempt.

title: Implement the frozen E01 bwrap runner
description:
## Outcome

Implement typed launch policies and the exact Linux `bwrap` runner frozen by E01 for the first Change pilot.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trusted evaluator and candidate launch types cannot be confused.
- [ ] The runner implements E01's mount, namespace, environment, path, resource, output, timeout, cancellation, and reaping contract without weakening it.
- [ ] Network, credentials, agent sockets, daemon sockets, host services, and unrelated host paths are unavailable.
- [ ] Unsupported host capability fails preflight instead of selecting a weaker fallback.
- [ ] Timeout, cancellation, crash, and blocked output kill and reap the full process group before cleanup.

title: Materialize and preflight the exact Git base
description:
## Outcome

Materialize and preflight the exact trusted Git base for the selected pilot grammar.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The base commit and tree are resolved from trusted configuration and verified before use.
- [ ] Candidate workspaces are fresh and cannot mutate the trusted repository or shared state.
- [ ] Unsupported submodules, links, special files, filters, hooks, attributes, or path forms fail preflight unless explicitly allowed by the pilot grammar.
- [ ] Build and test commands are fixed trusted inputs, not repository-supplied workflow code.

title: Fold Linux isolation into the runner
description:
## Disposition

Folded into `ravel-amn.1`. The MVP uses one concrete Linux runner, so launch lifecycle and isolation policy must be implemented and tested together.

title: Validate the delta and construct the Git candidate
description:
## Outcome

Validate the bounded filesystem delta and construct an immutable Git candidate from accepted bytes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The delta contains only regular files within the admitted write scope and size/count limits.
- [ ] Unexpected deletion, rename, mode, link, special file, escape, or generated output fails closed.
- [ ] Validation digests the exact accepted bytes before Git construction.
- [ ] The Git tree and commit are built without untrusted hooks, filters, configuration, credentials, or timestamps.
- [ ] Candidate identity binds base, delta digest, plan revision, work revision, and attempt.

title: Fold Git construction into delta validation
description:
## Disposition

Folded into `ravel-amn.4`. Delta validation and immutable Git construction share one byte-level trust boundary and should not drift as separate tasks.

title: Publish and reconstruct the candidate bundle
description:
## Outcome

Publish a bounded Git bundle and verify exact reconstruction on another worker.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The bundle contains only the required candidate objects and stays within the admitted artifact cap.
- [ ] Artifact publication uses content identity and scoped effect authority.
- [ ] A second worker reconstructs the expected commit and verifies commit, tree, base, and bundle digests.
- [ ] Missing, extra, corrupt, or mismatched objects fail closed.

## Artifact-record contract (folded from ravel-6pv)

- [ ] The bundle reference enters authoritative history only through the canonical
  scoped-v2 artifact-reference event, minted from a verified publication witness
  (`PublishedArtifact` in `src/storage/artifacts.rs`, metadata `ArtifactRef` in
  `src/domain/artifact.rs`), with its payload type registered in
  `payload_type_registered` (`src/scope.rs`).
- [ ] Publication and replay agree on the exact supported artifact record type — one
  shared definition, round-trip tested — and replay rebuilds bundle artifact metadata
  deterministically (`src/sync/replay.rs`, `src/db/projections.rs`).
- [ ] Malformed, unpublished, unsupported, or wrong-scope artifact references fail before
  the scope head advances, with a negative test per rejection class.
- [ ] Frozen v1 conversion behavior and `tests/wire.rs` fixtures are unchanged.
notes: Folded from ravel-6pv (closed, superseded): scoped-v2 must own the artifact record it admits. The FIRST of ravel-85q.2 / ravel-amn.6 / ravel-e1n.5 to land defines the ONE canonical artifact-reference payload type (registered in payload_type_registered, built on ArtifactRef/PublishedArtifact); the others reuse it and must not fork a second artifact record type.

title: Extend the Versioned Campaign Head as the Sole Authority Record
description:
## Context

E05 requires controller ownership and authoritative event publication to share one Amazon S3 campaign-head CAS domain. This task establishes the record that later acquisition, renewal, takeover, readiness, and event-commit work will use.

The pilot must keep the durable design narrow: one versioned head, one head key, and no independent controller record.

## Current State

The repository currently contains `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/epics.md`, `docs/mvp-outline.md`, and Beads metadata; it has no Rust source yet. `docs/epics.md` E05 AC1 and `docs/mvp-outline.md` §§6–7 define the combined authority/tail record. This task starts after E02 has created the single `ravel` package/node binary, the versioned event/head envelope, canonical encoding, opaque ETags, and the one campaign-head key. E01's private pilot configuration remains fixed and gains no schema or migration machinery here.

## Desired State

E02 (ravel-aq8.2) already froze the complete v1 head superset: explicit `Unowned | Owned { owner, instance, lease_until, controller_fence }`, authoritative event-tail sequence/digest/key, and the operation identity of the head mutation that produced it. This task adds no fields and changes no v1 bytes. It implements validation and authority-state transitions over those frozen fields: candidate replacements fail closed if they regress fence or tail or contain an invalid field combination.

There is no `controller.json`, second authoritative key, or duplicate envelope framework. The head operation ID is not implicitly reused as the next event commit's operation ID.

## Implementation Guidance

- Build on the frozen types in `src/sync/head.rs` without modifying the v1 byte contract; expose controller-facing validated values through `src/distributed/controller.rs` only as needed.
- Reuse E02's version tag, canonical encoding/decoding, unknown-version failure, opaque ETag type, and single head-key constant.
- Model only the owned and unowned states required by E05. Reject malformed partial authority, invalid tail metadata, lower replacement fences, and tail regression.
- Keep controller authority and event tail in the same serialized object and replacement validation path.
- Do not add a generic schema layer, migration framework, controller record, or source-layout test that is more brittle than the behavior it protects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controller validation covers the frozen head fields — owner/instance, lease, monotonic fence, event-tail sequence/digest/key, and operation identity — in one validated object, with no change to the E02 v1 byte contract and no added fields. (E05 AC1)
- [ ] The initial/unowned and owned states round-trip through E02's canonical envelope and invalid field combinations fail closed. (E05 AC1)
- [ ] Candidate head replacement rejects a lower controller fence and a regressing or internally inconsistent event tail. (E05 AC3 support)
- [ ] The implementation reuses one E02 campaign-head key and introduces no separately authoritative controller object or CAS path. (E05 AC1–AC2)
- [ ] Unknown envelope versions continue to fail before conversion to controller domain values. (E05 AC1)
- [ ] No schema/migration framework or portable storage abstraction is added.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** round-trip focused owned/unowned values; reject malformed authority/tail combinations and fence/tail regression.
- **Fixture:** reuse E02's frozen unowned/owned head fixtures unchanged; do not duplicate E02's full malformed-envelope matrix.
- **Live integration:** none in this task; E02 owns generic live head encoding/CAS coverage and E05's cross-host proof is separately gated.
- **Manual review:** confirm one head-key constant, one authoritative head representation, and no `controller.json` or parallel CAS domain.

## Design Gate
Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §7, §6; decomposed from epic ravel-8zo via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e05-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

## Final Step

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.
