title: Precommit the budgeted A/B/C experiments and record pilot identity
description:
## Context

E01 must precommit the Research and Change comparisons before measured pilot runs. A/B/C labels alone are insufficient because agent counts, assignment, visibility, communication, integration, reset semantics, treatment order, stopping, and treatment of failed runs can materially change the experiment.

This task also closes the private pilot configuration with fixed scalar budgets and immutable Git/content identity. It must use direct repository tools, not create a bundle subsystem, schema, validator, statistics framework, or runtime machinery.

## Current State

The repository has no runtime code or experiment framework. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §32 fixes the Research and Change treatments and measurement sets; §3 defers statistical performance search and generic workflow machinery; §43 requires bounded recursive work, hard budget enforcement, final rediscovery, actual multi-machine execution, and failover.

Task 1 provides the frozen environment, authority, trust roots, numeric repository limits, and passing preflight. Task 2 provides `pilot/e01/research.md` with the blinded reference/grading contract. Task 3 provides the fixed Change treatment, trusted discovery/evaluators, scopes, fixtures, target inventory, and final rediscovery rule. There are no prior-epic runtime outputs.

## Desired State

Create:

- `pilot/e01/budgets.yaml`
- `pilot/e01/experiments.md`

`budgets.yaml` contains fixed numeric caps for the eight E01 resource dimensions and explicit hard-limit behavior. `experiments.md` fully specifies all six Research/Change A/B/C cells, the treatment schedule, experimental and analysis units, isolation/reset rules, outcomes/calculations, and success/failure/inconclusive decisions. After committing all `pilot/e01/` artifacts, record the final Git revision, direct content digest, and one clean-checkout smoke result in task completion evidence outside the hashed directory.

## Implementation Guidance

Keep budgets flat. Give a numeric value and unit for exactly these mandatory dimensions:

1. calls or tokens
2. attempts
3. parallelism
4. generated follow-ups
5. workflow depth
6. deadlines
7. artifact size
8. total campaign spend or usage

Add a subordinate scalar only when one selected pilot concretely needs it to make a mandatory cap enforceable. Do not create campaign/workflow/work-item/provider/oracle budget hierarchies by default. At a hard limit, stop creating new work, allow required cleanup/reconciliation, and emit an explicit unresolved result. Do not permit silent or human-approved expansion during a run; changed caps require a new precommitment identity.

In `experiments.md`, create separate Research and Change tables with rows for A, B, and C. Every cell must fix:

- Exact input, source revision, contract/discovery/evaluator identities, provider/model roles, and budget reference.
- Exact agent count and machine count/topology.
- Work/target assignment and what each agent can see.
- Permitted communication and coordination.
- Integration behavior.
- Workspace, candidate, cache, and external-state isolation.
- Reset semantics between complete runs.
- Fixed integer run count.
- Measured outcomes, units, and calculation rules from §32.
- Success, failure, and inconclusive criteria.

Define the treatment/application unit and analysis unit. Use a complete assigned run as the independent unit unless another unit is explicitly justified; nested targets, work items, or conclusions are not independent replicates merely because there are many of them.

Use a seed-recorded blocked/counterbalanced schedule across A/B/C, or document a justified fixed-order model. Name nuisance-state blocks such as machine pool, time window, provider quota state, or source reset. State a fixed run-count sensitivity/power rationale and a complete-unit stopping rule. Do not adapt run count or stop after seeing favorable results. Crashes, errors, and timeouts remain assigned treatment outcomes and are not discarded, retried as fresh observations, or silently replaced.

Name one primary outcome family and success rule per pilot. Keep remaining §32 outcomes descriptive unless a multiplicity rule is predeclared. This task must not create a benchmark/statistics framework.

Research grading must reference only `pilot/e01/research.md`. Change correctness and completeness must reference only Task 3 discovery/evaluators/final rediscovery, not treatment self-report. Distributed C must require at least three independent machines/VM hosts and explicit controller failover evidence; subprocesses on one host do not qualify.

Mark the configuration private and unstable. Amendments require a new Git revision and content digest before affected runs; do not pool old and amended results silently.

After the files are committed, record these commands and outputs in task completion evidence, not under `pilot/e01/`:

```bash
git rev-parse HEAD
git ls-files -z pilot/e01 \
  | LC_ALL=C sort -z \
  | xargs -0 sha256sum \
  | sha256sum
```

The digest covers the sorted tracked path-and-content checksum list and cannot self-reference because no digest file is inside `pilot/e01/`. From a clean checkout at that revision, run Task 1 preflight and Task 3 discovery/fixture smoke, and record the reproduced revision, rule digest, and target count. Use manual diff review; do not add a bundle assembler, integrity-manifest format, custom validator, or prohibited-term scanner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pilot/e01/budgets.yaml` gives a numeric value and unit for all eight mandatory cap dimensions. **(E01 AC5)**
- [ ] Each hard limit stops new work, permits only required cleanup/reconciliation, and emits an explicit unresolved result; there is no silent or approval-driven expansion. **(E01 AC5/AC7)**
- [ ] Any subordinate cap is justified by a concrete selected-pilot need; no speculative budget hierarchy exists. **(E01 AC5/AC8)**
- [ ] `pilot/e01/experiments.md` fixes inputs, revision/digests, exact agent and machine counts, assignments/visibility, communication, integration, isolation/reset, run count, outcomes/calculations, and decision rules for all six A/B/C cells. **(E01 AC6)**
- [ ] Treatment/application units, analysis units, and interference boundaries are explicit; nested targets/conclusions are not treated as independent runs. **(E01 AC6)**
- [ ] A seed-recorded blocked/counterbalanced schedule or justified fixed-order model, nuisance blocks, run-count rationale, and fixed complete-unit stopping rule are precommitted. **(E01 AC6)**
- [ ] Crashes, errors, and timeouts remain assigned outcomes; they are not discarded or silently replaced. **(E01 AC6)**
- [ ] Each pilot has one primary outcome family and fixed success/failure/inconclusive rule; secondary measurements are descriptive or have a predeclared multiplicity rule. **(E01 AC6)**
- [ ] Research grading references the Task 2 contract, and Change correctness/completeness references the Task 3 trusted discovery/evaluators and zero-target final rediscovery. **(E01 AC1/AC2/AC6)**
- [ ] Distributed C requires at least three independent machines/VM hosts and records controller failover evidence. **(E01 AC6 and §43 invariant 20)**
- [ ] Routine treatment execution and safe-branch Change integration contain no human approval gate; post-hoc grading remains measurement. **(E01 AC7)**
- [ ] The final Git revision and external content digest are recorded, and one clean-checkout smoke reproduces preflight, discovery rule digest, fixture results, and target count. **(E01 AC8)**
- [ ] The final diff contains only private `pilot/e01/` artifacts and no schema migration system, profile registry, policy/workflow DSL, public configuration API, generic workflow/evaluator/backend infrastructure, custom validator/scanner, or runtime module. **(E01 AC8)**

## Testing Strategy

title: Reconstruct Disposable Local State from Durable History
description:
## Description

Build the per-node SQLite projection needed for synchronization and the next scheduling milestones. S3 remains the only durable authority. SQLite and the digest-addressed local artifact directory are disposable local accelerators and are never copied between machines.

A node rebuilds by reading a fresh campaign head and traversing immutable parent references, not by treating S3 prefix listing as a publication snapshot. Remote I/O and digest verification happen outside short database transactions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A fresh node reconstructs the campaign from the head by traversing the complete immutable parent chain; `LIST` is reserved for diagnosis or orphan accounting.
- [ ] Event bytes are fetched, version-validated, and digest-verified before opening the apply transaction.
- [ ] One transaction validates the next sequence and previous digest, applies all event-derived changes, records the unique event identity, and advances the `(sequence, tail_digest)` cursor.
- [ ] Reapplying the same event is a no-op. A gap, conflicting digest, unknown version, or failed conversion leaves both projection and cursor unchanged and makes readiness fail closed.
- [ ] The projector exposes its verified cursor against a freshly read S3 head. At the same cursor, all event-derived query state is equivalent; cache occupancy, advisory presence, and other ephemeral metadata are excluded.
- [ ] One daemon-owned writer task/connection serializes SQLite writes. No transaction or database guard crosses an `.await`, network work stays outside transactions, and blocking SQLite work does not run on async executor threads.
- [ ] The initial implementation uses serialized/default-journal access. WAL is enabled only after measured reader blocking justifies it, with one-host sidecars, writer-owned checkpointing, bounded busy handling, and verification of the linked SQLite version.
- [ ] The minimal schema has an explicit application/schema version and `NOT NULL` or `UNIQUE` constraints for stable identities, applied events, and cursors. If foreign keys are used, every connection enables and verifies them; rebuilt test databases pass `quick_check` and `foreign_key_check`.
- [ ] Only event/cursor and scheduling tables required by the current milestone are created; Research, Change, judgment, and evaluation tables arrive with their owning epics, with no generic projector, checkpoint, or cache-metadata framework.
- [ ] SQLite contains no uniquely durable state. Version or integrity mismatch stops local users and rebuilds from S3 instead of invoking online/rollback migrations, backup transport, or power-loss durability machinery.
- [ ] Kill and injected-write-failure tests cover before apply, after row mutation but before commit, and immediately after commit; recovery never skips or duplicates an event and never reports controller readiness from an invalid projection.

title: Fence Campaign Authority and Controller Failover
description:
## Description

Make controller ownership and event publication one atomic CAS domain. The campaign head contains controller owner, lease, fence, event tail, and operation identity together. Acquisition, renewal, takeover, and every authoritative event commit conditionally replace that same object, preventing a stale controller from publishing through an independently observed log-head ETag.

Keep policy separate from authority: deterministic policy proposes transitions from immutable observations, while the fenced authority layer performs and validates S3 changes. The top-level node supervisor owns all long-lived loops, spawned tasks, and bounded admission points.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controller owner, lease, monotonic fence, event tail, and operation identity reside in one versioned campaign-head object.
- [ ] Acquisition, renewal, takeover, and event publication all CAS the same observed head ETag; authoritative commit APIs require an opaque controller-authority value and revalidate it in that CAS.
- [ ] Event commits preserve the exact parent chain and cannot regress the controller fence. A stale controller cannot commit after a higher fence has won, even if it retained an older head observation.
- [ ] Before its first authoritative decision, a replacement controller rebuilds and verifies its projection to the exact freshly read S3 head. Gaps, unknown versions, and chain failures prevent readiness.
- [ ] Controller policy performs no S3 or provider I/O and cannot bypass the fenced commit layer; it only proposes deterministic state transitions.
- [ ] Killing the active controller allows another host to take over, process sealed submissions, and continue unexpired claims without requiring the old host to return.
- [ ] The node supervisor bounds every local admission queue and owns every renewal, sync, scheduling, invocation, and publication task. No detached task survives its owner.
- [ ] Shutdown stops admission, requests loop cancellation, classifies interrupted remote effects as known or unknown, performs required reconciliation, and joins or reaps all tasks before exit.
- [ ] Fault tests include lost head-CAS success followed by supersession, a delayed stale-controller write after takeover, takeover from stale SQLite, failure during submission processing, and restart reconciliation with no eager orphan deletion.

title: Establish the S3 Durable Log and Minimal Rust Runtime
description:
## Description

Create one Cargo package producing one node binary and implement the narrow Amazon S3 correctness boundary used by the campaign: immutable create-if-absent objects and one conditionally replaced campaign head. Events and artifacts are immutable; publication authority resides only in the head. The implementation uses the selected AWS SDK directly and does not hide S3 behind a portable object-store abstraction.

Durable records use one explicit v1 event/head envelope and canonical bytes. The campaign is append-only for the MVP: retained history, leaked orphan objects, and bounded single-request artifacts are preferable to unsafe cleanup, compaction, or multipart machinery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pinned Rust toolchain, edition, async runtime, target set, and locked dependency set build one binary; CI runs formatting, check, clippy with warnings denied, and tests without repository credentials.
- [ ] Immutable events and artifacts are created with `If-None-Match: *`; initial head creation uses the same precondition; head replacement uses `If-Match` with the observed ETag.
- [ ] ETags are treated only as opaque version tokens. Existing immutable keys are accepted only after trusted full-byte SHA-256 and size verification.
- [ ] The versioned envelope records stable commit/operation identity, sequence, parent sequence/digest/key, writer fence, and canonical content; unknown versions or invalid encodings fail closed before conversion to domain types.
- [ ] A frozen v1 history fixture proves decode, digest, and chain behavior without introducing a schema framework.
- [ ] Ambiguous publication checks the current head and, if superseded, walks the complete retained parent chain for the operation identity. A gap remains `UNRESOLVED`, and no object is eagerly deleted.
- [ ] Two processes racing from one observed head produce at most one authoritative publication; stale ETags, duplicate puts, timeout/reset, lost success, and an ambiguous retry followed by `409` or `412` cannot corrupt the chain.
- [ ] Live integration tests against the selected general-purpose S3 bucket and pinned SDK exercise typed `404`, `409`, `412`, timeout/reset, and lost-response behavior. Publication retries are disabled or proven to preserve identical bytes, preconditions, and operation identity.
- [ ] A lower fixture fence cannot replace a higher-fence head; dynamic controller acquisition and stale-controller takeover are deferred to the controller-authority epic.
- [ ] Event, artifact, and head prefixes have no application deletion, GC, compaction, or lifecycle expiration. Pilot artifacts stay below the single-`PutObject` limit; multipart upload is deferred.

title: Fix the Pilot and Experiment Contracts
description:
## Description

Choose the two controlled pilots before building runtime machinery: one evidence-rich Research question and one finite Change migration with a trusted discovery rule, one fixed treatment, and several dozen targets. Check in private, unstable pilot configuration that fixes trust boundaries, safe repositories and branches, provider profiles, evaluator commands, scalar budgets, and precommitted experiment criteria.

The configuration is an input to the MVP, not a new product surface. It is versioned by Git revision and content digest and uses fixed enums, allowlists, and bounds rather than a policy language or compatibility framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Research question has independently inspectable evidence and a defined method for assessing supported, incorrect, omitted, and unresolved conclusions.
- [ ] The Change migration has trusted deterministic discovery, one fixed treatment, explicit write scopes, several dozen targets, and few or no subjective exemptions.
- [ ] The pilot repository passes a Linux preflight and excludes unsupported repository constructs and candidate-controlled evaluator or workflow paths.

- [ ] Inputs, run counts, outcomes, and success criteria are precommitted for the single-agent, single-machine multi-agent, and distributed treatments.
- [ ] Routine Research decisions and safe-branch Change integration are autonomous; any human-only boundary is explicit and outside ordinary pilot progress.
- [ ] The configuration format is private and unstable. No schema migration system, profile registry, policy DSL, public configuration API, or generic workflow infrastructure is introduced.

title: Fence Work Claims and Result Submission
description:
## Description

Implement simple authoritative work claims separately from campaign-controller authority. A configured actor ID and random per-start instance ID identify a claimant; advisory presence publishes only static capabilities and lease freshness. Presence may improve routing but never proves ownership or drives correctness.

Each work claim is its own S3 CAS domain. Claiming, renewal, reclamation, and submission all transition the same claim object so completion cannot race reclamation through a different key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Stable actor identity and ephemeral instance identity are distinct, and every claim binds both identities, the work revision, and a monotonic fence.
- [ ] Presence contains actor, instance, static capabilities, and freshness only; stale or missing presence cannot violate ownership or block recovery.
- [ ] Claim creation, renewal, and reclamation use create-if-absent or `If-Match` on the same claim key, with one frozen lease policy and no generic membership or lease framework.
- [ ] Internal execute/submit APIs require an opaque fence-bearing claim authority value rather than accepting raw IDs supplied by a worker.
- [ ] Completion performs a same-key CAS from `ACTIVE(fence)` to `SEALED/SUBMITTED(fence, result_ref)`; reclamation and completion race on that ETag, and only one can win.
- [ ] A controller records only sealed submissions whose immutable result identity and work revision validate. A stale result may remain as evidence but cannot complete work.
- [ ] Two machines racing for a claim cannot both hold valid authority, and a lower-fence or wrong-revision submission fails closed.
- [ ] Unexpired claims remain valid across controller replacement and their sealed submissions can be processed by the replacement.
- [ ] Fault tests cover lost claim/renewal/submission responses, completion racing reclamation, worker death, a delayed old-fence return, and restart reconciliation without a machine-departure event.

title: S3 write path: authoritative group commit
description:
## Outcome

Amortize per-event write cost: build several events -> publish once -> single head CAS -> acknowledge the whole batch atomically. Flush by size or max delay; acknowledge only after durable publication (no memory-only acks; no extra WAL). One PR. Depends on the read-path task (replay ladder must consume batched history).

## Hard invariants

- Group commit is the one authoritative-format change: updates the single canonical contract, canonical bytes, and fixtures together — no second era, no compat decoder.
- `head` + `events/` remain the commitment authority.
- Ambiguity handling extends the existing commit protocol: lost-response reconciliation walks the (possibly batched) chain for the operation identity, exactly as today.

## Design fork (resolved in-pipeline by judge lane)

(a) N individual event PUTs + one head CAS advancing past all N (no layout change, CAS amortized only) vs (b) one immutable authoritative segment object holding the batch (fewer PUTs, but the durable-format change — canonical contract + fixtures updated together). Judge decides on evidence; rust-code-reviewer + ponytail-review sign off; rationale in bead notes.

## Acceptance

- Batch atomic at the head (all-or-nothing).
- Two racing committers -> at most one wins.
- Lost CAS response reconciles correctly.
- Replay (read-path ladder) consumes batched history identically.
- Fixtures per chosen option; live suite green (`RAVEL_LIVE_S3=1 cargo test --locked -- --ignored --test-threads=1`).

title: S3 replay read path: LIST-assisted fetch, packed segments, certified checkpoints
description:
## Outcome

Replace the serial per-object replay walk with a fail-closed accelerator ladder: certified checkpoint -> packed segments -> LIST-assisted concurrent fetch -> current serial walk. One PR.

## Hard invariants (into spec + every reviewer preamble)

- `head` + `events/` remain the commitment authority. Accelerator objects (packs, index, checkpoints) never required for correctness; fail-closed ladder: checkpoint -> packs -> LIST-assisted -> current serial walk.
- LIST is a hint, never a snapshot: pin head first, reconstruct the exact chain ending at it, ignore sequences beyond it, fall back on any gap/invalid candidate.
- Packs embed exact stored `.cbor.zst` bytes (no re-encode); every event re-verified by existing digest + canonical decoder.
- No deletion/GC/compaction of any prefix. Immutable objects use `If-None-Match: *`; only `replay-index/current` is CAS-replaced (accelerator-only).

## Scope

1. LIST-assisted concurrent replay (immediate win, permanent fallback rung): pin head -> paginated LIST -> filter <= pinned sequence -> bounded-concurrency GETs -> exact chain reconstruction -> serial-walk fallback.
2. Packed segments + index: `scopes/{scope}/replay-packs/{start}-{end}-{digest}`, `replay-index/{digest}` (immutable catalog), `replay-index/current` (CAS pointer). Pack = scope_id, start/end sequence, parent/tail refs, count, offset table, exact event bytes, checksum. Flush at 8 MiB OR 256 events (256 KiB max event bounds worst case). Producer: any node with fresh verified replay state, opportunistic post-replay, create-if-absent; CAS losers skip — read-side validation is the correctness boundary, no producer lease. Reader shared by replay and the ambiguous-commit reconciliation walk (closes deferred ravel-lj0); validates every event, boundary, sequence, parent digest, epoch, operation identity, and final tail against the pinned head. Referenced plans/artifacts fetched concurrently, deduped by digest.
3. Certified checkpoints: `scopes/{scope}/checkpoints/{sequence}-{digest}`. Certification = fenced `ProjectionCheckpointPublished` event committing snapshot digest + covered `(sequence, tail_digest)` cursor (authority stays in the event log). Loader validates scope, covered cursor, active-plan binding, application ID, format, and SQLite `quick_check`/`foreign_key_check` before atomic install; retains log + one older checkpoint. Cold replay: pin head -> newest compatible checkpoint -> pack-fetch suffix -> validate tail. Checkpoints never substitute for retained-history ambiguity searches — packs cover those.

## Acceptance

- Projection/cursor equivalence vs serial walk from genesis AND from checkpoint at the same pinned head.
- Corrupt/wrong-scope/tail-mismatch packs and uncertified/mismatched snapshots fail closed down the ladder.
- Interrupted checkpoint install leaves prior projection intact.
- Orphans/gaps -> fallback; flush limits enforced; duplicate publication idempotent; CAS-race loser harmless.
- Reconciliation-over-packs equals per-event walk.
- Request waves drop (~N -> ~N/256; checkpointed cold start ~= 1 + suffix/256).
- Fixtures + live suite green (`RAVEL_LIVE_S3=1 cargo test --locked -- --ignored --test-threads=1`).

## Final step

Close ravel-lj0 with reference to this task.

title: Batch the replay suffix into one SQLite worker command and one transaction
description:
# Batch the replay suffix into one SQLite worker command and one transaction

## Context

`sync::replay` already holds the complete validated suffix in memory (`PreparedSuffix`, bounded by `LIMITS = 4_096 events / 64 MiB`, `src/sync/replay.rs:35`). Yet application to the SQLite projection is per event: N `scope_conflicting_operation` queue round trips, then N `handle.apply()` round trips (each opening its own transaction), then a final `scope_matches_head` round trip. A mid-suffix database failure leaves a committed prefix — intentional today, but the projection is disposable, so all-or-nothing is the simpler correctness model. Review verdict: the per-event application shape is accidental, not designed.

Benefits: one queue round trip, one SQLite transaction, no separate conflict-query pass, whole suffix applies or rolls back, simpler correctness model.

## Current State

```rust
// src/sync/replay.rs:269-330 (abridged) — per-event application
pub(crate) async fn apply_suffix(
    handle: &DbHandle,
    scope: &ScopeIdentity,
    mut prepared: PreparedSuffix,
) -> Result<((u64, Digest), ObservedScopeHead), ScopeReplayError> {
    for event in &prepared.events {
        if handle.scope_conflicting_operation(scope, /* op id, ref */).await? // N round trips
        { return Err(ScopeReplayError::HistoryConflict); }
    }
    // ...convert to Vec<ScopeProjectionEvent> mutations...
    for mutation in mutations {
        match handle.apply(mutation).await {                                 // N round trips, N txns
            Ok(ApplyOutcome::Applied | ApplyOutcome::AlreadyApplied) => {}
            Err(error) => return Err(ScopeReplayError::Apply(error)),
        }
    }
    if !handle.scope_matches_head(prepared.observed.head()).await? // 1 more round trip
    { return Err(ScopeReplayError::HistoryConflict); }
    // cursor derived from observed head
}
```

```rust
// src/db/projections.rs:1212-1216 — each apply opens its own transaction
pub(crate) fn apply_scope_event(
    connection: &mut rusqlite::Connection,
    event: &ScopeProjectionEvent,
) -> Result<ApplyOutcome, ApplyError> {
    let transaction = connection.transaction()?;
    // conflict/idempotency checks + INSERT + scopes cursor/tail advance
```

`Command` enum in `src/db/worker.rs:40` has per-event `Apply`, plus `ConflictingOperation`, `MatchesHead`. The worker owns one connection on a blocking thread; `DbHandle::enqueue` is the single queue entry point.

Production callers (verified):
- `handle.apply` — ONLY `src/sync/replay.rs:315`; all other uses are tests.
- `scope_conflicting_operation` — ONLY replay's pre-pass (`src/sync/replay.rs:290`); rest are tests.
- `scope_matches_head` — replay AND `src/distributed/grants.rs:258` (must stay a production command).

## Desired State

One new worker command applies the whole suffix in one transaction:

```rust
handle.apply_suffix(scope, mutations, observed_head).await
```

Worker side (single `Command::ApplySuffix`), inside ONE `rusqlite` transaction:

1. For each mutation in order: the per-event conflict/idempotency checks and row writes that `apply_scope_event` performs today, executed against the shared transaction. `AlreadyApplied` skips and continues (preserves idempotent re-replay from an older cursor). Any `Conflict`/error → roll back the entire suffix.
2. After all events: the `scope_matches_head` predicate evaluated in the same transaction; mismatch → roll back, `Conflict`.
3. Commit. Cursor advance is inherent — each event's apply already updates `scopes.sequence`/`tail_event_digest`; after commit the cursor equals the observed head.

`replay::apply_suffix` collapses to: convert prepared events → one `handle.apply_suffix(...)` call → return cursor. The separate conflict pre-pass loop, per-event apply loop, and post-hoc head check are deleted.

**Simplicity gate:** minimum viable change — extend the existing `Command` enum and refactor `apply_scope_event`'s body to run against a caller-provided transaction (e.g. take `&rusqlite::Transaction` or split an inner fn). No new module, no new abstraction, no chunking machinery: the suffix is already bounded at 4,096 events / 64 MiB by `prepare_suffix` limits, well within a single SQLite transaction. Chunking (fixed 128–256) only if the sqlite-review pre-check stage demands it with a concrete reason.

Demotions (repo pattern — `#[cfg(test)]` commands like `AdmitWork`/`RecordGrant`, `src/db/worker.rs:61-79`):
- `Command::Apply` + `DbHandle::apply` → `#[cfg(test)]` (tests at worker.rs:880-1139 still exercise queue-full/contention paths through it).
- `Command::ConflictingOperation` + `DbHandle::scope_conflicting_operation` → `#[cfg(test)]`.
- `MatchesHead` stays production (grants.rs:258).

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `src/db/worker.rs` | Add `Command::ApplySuffix` + `DbHandle::apply_suffix`; demote `Apply`/`ConflictingOperation` to `#[cfg(test)]` | Single queue round trip |
| `src/db/projections.rs` | Refactor `apply_scope_event` to run against a shared transaction; add `apply_scope_suffix(connection, events, head) -> Result<(), ApplyError>` that wraps loop + head check + commit | Single transaction, all-or-nothing |
| `src/sync/replay.rs` | Collapse `apply_suffix` to conversion + one handle call | Delete the accidental per-event shape |

### Existing Code to Reuse

Duplication check ran on "apply a batch of projection events in one SQLite transaction through the worker queue" (inline colgrep/grep pass, code-quality plugin degrade path).

**Outcome: EXTEND**

- `src/db/worker.rs:40` `Command` enum — add one variant; do not build a second dispatch path.
- `src/db/projections.rs:1212` `apply_scope_event` — its conflict/idempotency/write logic is the per-event body; hoist the transaction out rather than duplicating the logic.
- `src/db/projections.rs:598` `scope_matches_head` — reuse the same predicate inside the batch transaction.

The implementing agent MUST start by reading these locations and confirm the verdict still holds at HEAD before writing new code.

### Patterns to Follow
- `#[cfg(test)]` command variants with doc comments naming the production writer (`src/db/worker.rs:61-79`).
- `apply_lookup_statements_avoid_table_scans` test (`src/db/projections.rs:1887`) — extend/keep green if SQL is touched.
- Bounded-queue behavior test shape (`src/db/worker.rs:834`).

### Blast Radius
- `src/sync.rs` calls replay's `apply_suffix` (line ~123) — signature unchanged if the replay-level fn keeps its shape; only internals collapse.
- `src/distributed/grants.rs:258` depends on `MatchesHead` — untouched.
- Rebuild path (`recovery/reconcile`, 5d2.3's rebuild) replays through the same fold — batch must handle every payload type in `typed_payload` (PlanAdmitted, RootGenesis, GrantActivated, test successor) with zero payload-specific changes.
- Worker tests using `handle.apply` (worker.rs:880, 914, 1048, 1056, 1139) and replay tests (replay.rs:645-1062, incl. the `LIMITS.events`-sized chain test) need mechanical updates.

## Code References

```rust
// src/sync/replay.rs:35-38 — suffix bound that makes single-txn safe
const LIMITS: Limits = Limits {
    events: 4_096,
    bytes: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
};
```

```rust
// src/db/worker.rs:41-44 — per-event command being demoted
Apply {
    mutation: Box<ScopeProjectionEvent>,
    respond: oneshot::Sender<Result<ApplyOutcome, ApplyError>>,
},
```

## Design Notes

- design-risk gate waived by invoker: mechanism (single txn batch over an already-bounded, already-in-memory suffix) was settled in the prior plan-mode session; bound is pre-existing (`LIMITS`), no new growth dimension, no new concurrency — worker stays single-connection single-thread.
- Deliberate semantics change: mid-suffix failure no longer leaves a committed prefix. Projection is disposable (rebuilt from durable facts per ravel-5d2.3), so atomic-suffix is strictly simpler; document this in the fn doc.
- Per-event `AlreadyApplied` tolerance inside the batch is REQUIRED — a crash between S3-head observation and cursor commit means the next replay re-sends an overlapping suffix.

## Testing Strategy

- Rollback atomicity: build a suffix where event k (k>1) conflicts (duplicate operation-id or tampered digest); assert Err, zero rows applied, cursor unchanged from pre-batch value.
- Idempotent overlap: apply a suffix, then re-apply from an older cursor including already-applied events plus new ones; assert Ok and final cursor == head.
- Head mismatch inside txn: suffix whose final state ≠ observed head → Err(Conflict), full rollback.
- Queue-full: `ApplySuffix` against a stalled worker reports `Full` (mirror worker.rs:834 test).
- Update existing replay tests (replay.rs:645+) and the 4,096-event chain test to the new API; the big-chain test now doubles as the single-large-transaction proof.
- One targeted mutation check per epic convention: hand-revert the head-match guard; a test must fail.

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| ravel-5d2 | Simplify scoped-work mental model (epic, closed children) | relates-to — this task came from the same mental-model review; verdict "per-event SQLite application looks accidental" |
| ravel-5d2.3 | Rebuild projection from durable facts (PR #51) | relates-to — branch stacks on `task/ravel-5d2.3`; batch fold must cover `grant_activated` |
| ravel-1nr | Projection authority mutations at execution time | relates-to, NOT in scope |

## Process (locked by user)

Pipeline per repo precedent (ravel-5d2 run), autonomous, no human input:
1. `bd update <id> --claim`; branch `task/<id>` stacked on `task/ravel-5d2.3`.
2. **Pre-check**: `/cloud-infra:sqlite-review` on this approach (single 4,096-event txn vs chunks; txn boundary; busy/WAL behavior). Disagreement → LLM-as-judge + `/rust-code-reviewer` + `/ponytail-review` sign-off, ruling recorded on the bead.
3. Spec stage (spec file + one critique pass) → `/implementation:rust-implementation` worker.
4. Verification: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`.
5. Review round: 4 parallel lanes — `/rust-code-reviewer`, `/less-code`, `/reduce-complexity`, `/invariant-test-review`; fix-and-rereview until all PASS.
6. Final gates: `/ponytail-review`, then `/doc-rigor`.
7. PR: push branch, `gh pr create` with base `task/ravel-5d2.3`; never merge. `bd close <id>`. STOP — no further tasks (user-confirmed single-task loop).
Factual questions → expert agent; design questions → judge protocol above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replay applies a suffix through exactly ONE `DbHandle` call; grep shows no production per-event apply loop or conflict pre-pass in `src/sync/replay.rs`.
- [ ] Whole-suffix atomicity test passes (mid-suffix conflict → zero rows, cursor unchanged).
- [ ] Idempotent-overlap test passes (`AlreadyApplied` inside batch).
- [ ] In-transaction head-match test passes (mismatch → full rollback).
- [ ] `Command::Apply` and `Command::ConflictingOperation` are `#[cfg(test)]`; `MatchesHead` unchanged (grants.rs:258 compiles untouched).
- [ ] No new helper/struct/trait beyond the one command + one batch fn — the existing code at worker.rs:40 / projections.rs:1212 is extended, not duplicated.
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test --locked`.
- [ ] Clean build: `cargo fmt --check && cargo check --locked && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`.
- [ ] No net increase in accidental complexity (`/reduce-complexity` lane in review round covers this; new HIGH/CRITICAL hotspots justified or fixed).

## Pointers

- `docs/workflows/beads.md` — claim/close/commit rules; commit `.beads/` export on the task branch.
- ravel-5d2.3 bead notes — design-ruling format precedent for the escalation path.
- `src/db/worker.rs:580` `fn run` — worker command dispatch loop where the new arm lands.
- `src/db/schema.rs` — no schema change expected; touch only if the batch fn needs a prepared-statement constant.
notes:
PHASE-1 SQLITE PRE-CHECK (code-only): ACCEPT single transaction; no chunks. Existing LIMITS of 4,096 events / 64 MiB already bounds the suffix before SQLite; peak memory is unchanged because replay already materializes it. Worker owns one DELETE-journal connection on one thread, so no in-process BUSY/WAL concern and no pragma change is authorized. Transaction opens after dequeue, stays entirely on worker thread, uses default deferred begin, evaluates conflict/idempotency + head predicate before commit, and returns one aggregate result. AlreadyApplied remains digest-at-sequence equality and continues through later events. Out-of-band writers/readers remain unsupported; a batch lengthens their immediate SQLITE_BUSY window, which current ApplyError flattening already reports as DatabaseOperationFailed.

DECISION: user-locked task semantics control head mismatch: mismatch is Conflict and rolls back whole suffix. Pre-check suggestion to preserve prefix is declined because task explicitly supersedes committed-prefix behavior; replay test/docs will be changed to prove atomic head-mismatch rollback. Keep pre-check safeguards: no chunking, no WAL/busy pragma work, no transaction across await.

Evidence: src/sync/replay.rs LIMITS / prepare-before-write, src/db/worker.rs single connection queue, src/db/projections.rs existing per-event transaction. Runtime SQLite version, batch journal growth, fsync and queue-latency measurements unavailable.

REVIEW ROUND 1 (commit 51d46bd): 4 parallel lanes all PASS. rust-code-reviewer: 0 blocker/major, 2 minor (doc wording) + 4 nit. less-code: -202 candidate lines, largest = full ConflictingOperation chain deletion. reduce-complexity: no new HIGH/CRITICAL hotspot; net accidental complexity negative. invariant-test-review: all 3 mandated mutations KILLED (head-check revert, commit-before-error, digest-equality weakening) plus 3 bonus mutations killed; kill matrix on record in lane artifact.

DECLINED (on record): (1) Conflict->HistoryConflict cause attribution — spec-locked unification, diagnostics-only. (2) CommittedProjectionBehind dedicated fixture test — narrow post-append takeover race, fail-closed, doc widened instead. (3) Deleting the full-limit test — bead testing strategy requires the 4,096-event proof through the new API; strengthened with suffix_count instead. (4) Deleting the recovery tail of a_database_failure_rolls_back_the_entire_suffix — it kills the inverted-head-check mutant and proves a rolled-back file replays. (5) epics.md E03 wording — historical proof record per spec. (6) Migrating remaining cfg(test) apply seeding to apply_suffix — deferred; would add test code today.

title: Persist the exact bindings scheduling depends on: dependency revision and grant deadline
description:
## Outcome

Every binding scheduling relies on is stored exactly, so no query has to guess which revision or which deadline it meant.

## Scope (items 3, 5)

3. work_dependencies gains depends_on_work_revision (primary key extended, FK and CHECKs per the existing repo pattern). Admission resolves each declared dependency (a WorkId in the proposal; proposal shape unchanged) to the exact WorkRef admitted by the same PlanRevision and stores it. Readiness requires terminal evidence on that exact (work_id, revision) row; a newer revision of the dependency does NOT satisfy it.
5. record_grant persists the grant real deadline_unix_ms (from EffectGrant) alongside the already-stored grant_digest, with presence/range CHECKs joined to the existing grant-column group. continuable_work filters expired grants at query time. The activation-time retest stays: defense in depth, not replaced.

## Acceptance

- Test: a dependency is satisfied only by its exact bound revision terminal evidence; a newer revision does not satisfy it.
- Test: continuable_work excludes a grant at deadline == now and includes at deadline > now.
- Test: schema CHECKs reject half-populated new columns.
- Full local CI command set green.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #50 (task/ravel-5d2.2, base main after #49 merged). work_dependencies.depends_on_work_revision (exact admission-time binding, PK-probe resolved arm), admitted_work.grant_deadline_unix_ms (5-column grant group, continuable_work filters expired grants). Review: 3 lanes + 10 mutations (2 initially surviving, both closed with new assertions), ponytail + doc-rigor PASS.

title: Rebuild every projection column from durable facts and take typed authority at authorization boundaries
description:
## Outcome

A rebuilt projection is scheduling-identical to the one it replaced, and no mutation is authorized by a bare integer.

## Scope (items 4, 6)

4. Every projection row/column is reconstructible from durable facts: PlanAdmitted events -> admitted_work + work_dependencies; durable claim objects -> claim_fence / claim_lease_until; durable grant records -> grant columns including the granted_units running total and the grant deadline; sealed submissions -> terminal_result_digest. Two candidate shapes, both named in ravel-m42: (a) new durable scope events for grant/claim/terminal facts replayed by sync::replay, or (b) rebuild reads the existing S3 claim/grant/submission objects at deterministic keys. The spec decides via the design-escalation path. Constraint either way: no prefix listing (repo invariant), and the fail-open granted_units reset from ravel-m42 is closed.
6. Authorization-bearing entry points (record_grant, record_claim, terminal recording, continuable_work, and any mutation that today takes scope_epoch: NonZeroU64 as its authorization input) take &ControllerAuthority or a typed token derived from it. scope_epoch params/columns remain only as provenance/consistency metadata: projection lag becomes a consistency error, never an authorization pass. Read-only observability queries may keep a raw epoch.

## Acceptance

- Round-trip property test: populate the projection (claims, grants across >= 2 fences, terminals), rebuild_projection, assert byte-identical scheduling-relevant rows including granted_units totals. This kills the ravel-m42 fail-open.
- Compile-level: no public mutation path accepts a bare epoch as authorization.
- Tests: a stopped or superseded ControllerAuthority is refused regardless of epoch; epoch lag surfaces as a consistency error.
- Full local CI command set green.

## Related

- ravel-m42 (grant accounting must survive a rebuild): closed with this task if fully covered, otherwise a residual note stays.
- ravel-1nr (enqueue-time clock): related, deliberately NOT in scope.
notes:
DESIGN RULING (LLM-judge escalation, per epic protocol): hybrid-with-modifications.
- grant_activated scope event appended by grants::issue, payload carries all five grant facts (fence, digest, attempt, units, deadline); replay applies it as an unconditional fold. Closes the ravel-m42 fail-open exactly (granted_units = ordered event fold).
- Claim columns (claim_fence, claim_lease_until) restored at rebuild by GET of the claim object at scope_claim_key (fence lives IN the object; no listing, no probe).
- Terminal half DEFERRED: record_terminal has no production writer; rebuild must not surface evidence production cannot record.
- Rejected: (a) all-events — workers hold no log-append authority; (b) all-objects — granted_units running total spans unaddressable historical fences, and object presence != activation (refused objects must stay inert).
Sign-offs: rust-code-reviewer APPROVED with 4 constraints (issue() consumes+returns refreshed ControllerAuthority; guards dry-run BEFORE append, fold unconditional after; pre-append operation-id probe against applied_scope_events; Sealed claim at rebuild = skip, leave NULL). ponytail-review APPROVED with 3 simplifications (deterministic round-trip test not proptest; no headroom-assertion machinery — replay Overflow is the bound; claim reader Active-arm only).
Artifacts: /tmp/dossier-ravel-5d2.3.md, /tmp/ruling-ravel-5d2.3.md
close_reason: Shipped as PR #51. grant_activated durable event (fold-based granted_units — kills the m42 fail-open), rebuild claim restore behind a claims_restored flag, typed authority on intake/continuable_work. Design escalation ruled hybrid (dossier+ruling+two sign-offs on the bead). 14 mutations all killed; round-2 wedge fix mutation-verified; ponytail+doc-rigor PASS.

title: Name scheduling queries for what they authorize and bind current revision to the active plan
description:
## Outcome

Scheduling reads say what they authorize, and "the current revision of work W" is an explicit durable binding to the scope active PlanRevision rather than an implicit SELECT MAX(work_revision).

- A superseded revision that holds a live claim or terminal evidence keeps its row for provenance but is not scheduled.
