title: Evaluate projection authority mutations at execution time, not enqueue time
description:
## Outcome

A projection mutation that changes authority is evaluated against the clock and authority current
when it executes, not when it was enqueued.

## Context

`DbHandle` commands carry a caller-supplied `now_ms` across an unbounded queue to a single SQLite
worker. `record_grant`'s SQL then tests `claim_lease_until > ?7` and `?6 > ?7` against that
enqueue-time reading, and `resumable_work` filters leases the same way.

`ravel-b8d.3` (PR #47) narrowed this twice and neither narrowing reaches the bottom:

- `issue` bounds publication and recording by one deadline and advances `now_ms` by elapsed time
  before enqueueing, but `tokio::time::timeout_at` only drops the response future. An accepted
  command still applies, so a mutation can commit after the controller's term ended while `issue`
  has already returned `Unresolved`.
- `intake` advances `now_ms` for every deadline check and retests the row's own
  `claim_lease_until` after the query returns, which closes the read side locally. The write side
  has no equivalent, because no local check can un-apply a committed row.

Found by the Codex reviewer across three rounds on PR #47
(`src/distributed/grants.rs:265`, `:282`, `:361`), each round correctly identifying the next layer.

## Desired State (minimum)

Pick one and apply it to every authority-changing projection command, not only grants:

1. Evaluate the clock inside the worker at execution time, which means the worker owns a clock
   rather than trusting a queued reading. Note that projection determinism from durable history
   must be preserved; `record_grant` is not event-driven, so the blast radius is bounded.
2. Make an enqueued mutation cancellable, so a dropped receiver or an expired term prevents
   application rather than merely abandoning the reply.
3. Carry an authority deadline in the command and refuse to apply past it, which pushes the same
   check into the worker without giving it a wall clock.

## Out of scope
Head revalidation after publication (eventless-takeover detection), which needs a store read and
belongs with launcher enforcement at execution entry (ravel-1rc).

## Acceptance criteria
- A mutation that reaches the worker after its authorizing term ends does not take effect.
- Grant activation cannot commit after `issue` has reported `Unresolved` for a term expiry.
- The chosen mechanism covers every authority-changing command, not just `record_grant`.
- A test drives a queued mutation past its authority deadline and asserts no row changed.
- fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, ignored gates clean.

title: Make grant accounting survive a projection rebuild
description:
## Outcome

Grant activation and cumulative budget consumption survive a projection rebuild.

## Context

`ravel-b8d.3` (PR #47) records grant activation only in SQLite: `record_grant` sets
`admitted_work.grant_fence`, `grant_digest`, and the `granted_units` running total, and no scope
event carries any of it. The projection is disposable by design — `sync::replay::open_projection`
calls `rebuild_projection`, which deletes the file and replays scope events
(`src/sync/replay.rs:132-165`) — and no replay path calls `record_grant`.

After a rebuild, or on a replacement host with no projection:

- Live grants become unresumable, because `grant_fence` is NULL. Fail-closed, but it silently
  revokes authority that was legitimately issued.
- `granted_units` resets to NULL. Fail-OPEN: the plan's `reserved_budget_units` can be drawn again
  in full, which defeats the ceiling b8d.3 added.

Found by the Codex reviewer on PR #47 (`src/db/projections.rs:92`), verified against
`rebuild_projection` and the `record_grant` call graph.

## Desired State (minimum)

Cumulative consumption is reconstructible from durable state, and the fail-open direction is
closed. Two candidate shapes, to be decided in this bead rather than assumed:

1. A grant-issued scope event, so replay reconstructs `grant_fence`/`grant_digest`/`granted_units`
   like any other projected state. Adds a payload type and a wire-compatibility step, and puts a
   durable append in the issuance path that today is one conditional-PUT plus one local UPDATE.
2. Reconstruct at replay from the grant objects themselves. This needs a LIST per scope, which
   b8d.3 deliberately avoided ("addressable without listing"), and object presence alone does not
   prove activation.

3. Refuse grant issuance on a rebuilt projection until consumption is reconstructed, which is the
   fail-closed interim CodeRabbit proposed on PR #47. It needs a durable marker distinguishing a
   rebuilt projection from a genuinely new one, and a rule for when the marker clears, so it is a
   decision rather than a one-line guard.

Whichever is chosen, a rebuild must not let a scope re-draw a reservation it already spent.

## Acceptance criteria
- A projection rebuild preserves cumulative grant consumption for every admitted revision.
- A rebuild cannot let a scope draw more than `reserved_budget_units` in total across all fences.
- The chosen mechanism states what happens to grants that were live at rebuild time.
- A test rebuilds a projection with a recorded grant and asserts consumption is not lost.
- fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, ignored gates clean.
close_reason: Closed by ravel-5d2.3 / PR #51, covering both named failure directions: granted_units is now an ordered fold over durable grant_activated scope events (fail-open closed — round-trip test pins the exact total across two fences after rebuild), and live grants survive rebuild because the grant columns replay from events while claim columns restore from the claim objects at their deterministic keys (unresumable-grant direction). Decision shape (a)-for-grants/(b)-for-claims recorded on ravel-5d2.3 with the dossier and ruling.

title: Run the root-only two-worker Change proof
description:
## Outcome

Run the root-only two-worker Change slice end to end before a product trial.

## Boundary

This is the MVP engineering proof. It does not consume E01's reserved treatment-C run. The deferred multi-host experiment remains `ravel-e1n.7`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The repository and objective satisfy the frozen E01 Change discovery, grouping, path, sandbox, budget, and evaluator contracts.
- [ ] One root controller admits target groups through `PlanRevision`; two workers use distinct claims and `EffectGrant` records against the same exact base.
- [ ] Worker cancellation is exercised separately from the normal run and does not corrupt authority, target accounting, or artifacts.
- [ ] Final trusted rediscovery classifies every current target.
- [ ] The local branch, bundle, report, evidence, and target accounting reconstruct on a fresh host.
- [ ] The run records elapsed time, provider usage and cost, interventions, retries, rejected work, and unresolved work.

title: Issue the MVP product decision
description:
## Outcome

Decide whether to continue, narrow, revise, or stop after the two product trials.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] State whether the partner received useful outcomes and chose repeat use.
- [ ] Identify the smallest blocking product or engineering gaps.
- [ ] Decide which deferred capability, if any, has earned implementation next.
- [ ] Keep the frozen E01 feasibility gate separate; product success does not count as its experimental proof.

title: Render the offline product scorecard
description:
## Outcome

Render one small offline scorecard from the two retained trial records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report baseline versus Ravel for elapsed time, user effort, cost, correctness, reviewability, interventions, retries, and unresolved work.
- [ ] Separate measured facts from user judgment and engineering interpretation.
- [ ] Do not add a metrics service, dashboard, experiment framework, or statistical claim.

title: Run a repeat-use product trial
description:
## Outcome

Run a second bounded Change objective to test repeat use rather than first-run novelty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same partner supplies a new objective without changing core architecture or success criteria.
- [ ] The run records the same measurements as the first trial.
- [ ] Any new product intervention or implementation work is classified and bounded.
- [ ] The partner states whether they would use the workflow again on comparable work.

title: Run the first supervised product outcome
description:
## Outcome

Run the selected objective with the design partner present and retain the complete reviewable result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The user supplies only the objective, bounds, and explicit interventions.
- [ ] Ravel returns the local branch, bundle, evidence, target accounting, cost, elapsed time, and stop reason.
- [ ] Every intervention and failed handoff is recorded.
- [ ] The partner reviews the result and records whether it is correct, understandable, and useful.

title: Select a design-partner objective and baseline
description:
## Outcome

Choose one real Change objective with a design partner before implementation is tuned to the case.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record the repository, objective, allowed scope, required checks, budget, and stop condition.
- [ ] Record how the partner performs the work today and the expected time and effort.
- [ ] Define reviewability, correctness, intervention, cost, and elapsed-time success criteria before the run.
- [ ] Confirm the repository fits the MVP preflight grammar; unsupported requirements are explicit.

title: Validate the MVP with design partners
description:
## Outcome

Validate that a design partner can give Ravel a bounded Change objective and receive a reviewable result worth using again.

## Boundary

This is a product-validation gate. It does not run or replace the frozen E01 A/B/C feasibility experiments and does not consume their reserved run IDs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One supervised outcome and one repeat-use trial complete against agreed objectives and bounds.
- [ ] Each trial records the manual baseline, elapsed time, cost, interventions, retries, rejected work, unresolved work, and review outcome.
- [ ] The final decision states whether the product solves a repeated user problem well enough to continue investment.

title: Provision the least-privilege live S3 identity
description:
## Outcome

Provision the least-privilege S3 identity used by live MVP nodes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The identity is restricted to the selected workspace, campaign, root-scope, plan, and artifact prefixes it needs.
- [ ] `DeleteObject`, lifecycle mutation, bucket administration, and unrelated prefixes are denied.
- [ ] Credentials are injected at runtime and never stored in plans, events, traces, bundles, or logs.
- [ ] Retained evidence proves required operations succeed and prohibited delete and cross-prefix operations fail.

title: E02 remediation: run doc-rigor + ponytail-review per task Final Step across aq8.1-aq8.8 and update all stacked PRs
description: Each ravel-aq8.x task's Final Step requires a /ponytail-review pass AND a /doc-rigor pass before close. Ponytail ran as a final gate for aq8.1-aq8.7; doc-rigor never ran. Remediation: for each task 1-8, run BOTH skills thoroughly against that task's final diff (previous-branch..task-branch), apply findings as commits on the task's own branch, merge forward through the stack (task/N -> task/N+1) so PRs #9-#16 all update. Verify full gates at each branch after merge-forward. Source: user directive during aq8.8.
close_reason: Done via the final-view approach the user directed: doc-rigor (writer + isolated verifier, 2 rounds, 118 claims) and a whole-repo ponytail pass ran against the aq8.8 tip, which contains all eight tasks' code; fixes landed on task/ravel-aq8.8 and updated PR #16. Residual judge-blocked doc nits filed separately.

title: Define the minimum Change workflow projection
description:
## Outcome

Define the minimum Change workflow projection and replay rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The projection separates target, admitted work, attempt, candidate, evidence, selection, and result state.
- [ ] Records bind root scope, plan digest, work revision, authority, and exact Git base.
- [ ] Workflow observations can propose a new plan revision but cannot create work or terminal state directly.
- [ ] Replay is deterministic and rejects impossible transitions before mutation.

title: Discover, group, and account for Change targets
description:
## Outcome

Apply the frozen E01 Change discovery and grouping contract, then account for every target through final rediscovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trusted discovery runs against the exact base with the frozen E01 rule and records its output digest.
- [ ] Target IDs use E01's `path:line:col:matched-line` digest and are stable only within that source revision; later movement is handled by trusted rediscovery.
- [ ] The first pilot uses E01's path-ordered, single-file grouping rule with a cap of 8 targets; the frozen repository produces the expected 16 groups.
- [ ] Unsupported or ambiguous targets become explicit `BLOCKED` or `UNRESOLVED` records.
- [ ] Final rediscovery maps every current target to resolved, rejected, blocked, or unresolved and reports every new or unmatched target.

title: Construct candidates on two workers
description:
## Outcome

Construct candidates concurrently on two workers against the declared base.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each target group is admitted work with its own revision, claim, and sandbox/Git grants.
- [ ] Workers receive only the objective, admitted context, exact base, write scope, commands, and bounds required for their group.
- [ ] Candidate creation uses the one-provider path and selected sandbox/Git pipeline.
- [ ] Concurrent candidates cannot see or mutate one another or the integration state.
- [ ] Late or stale-revision results remain auditable but are ineligible.

title: Gate selection and admit one retry
description:
## Outcome

Gate candidate selection on trusted evidence and allow at most one admitted retry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mechanical evidence must pass before semantic selection.
- [ ] Semantic selection is bounded, recorded as an attributed observation, and cannot override a mechanical failure.
- [ ] A retry requires a fresh `PlanRevision`, work revision, claim, grant, attempt, and candidate identity.
- [ ] The retry retains prior evidence and stays within the original campaign budget.
- [ ] No eligible candidate yields an explicit rejected or unresolved result.

title: Assemble the local review branch, bundle, and report
description:
## Outcome

Assemble accepted candidates into a reviewable local branch, bundle, and outcome report.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Candidates are applied serially against the current integration base with deterministic conflict handling.
- [ ] Each applied result reruns required trusted evaluation.
- [ ] The final branch and bundle bind the exact base, ordered candidates, final tree, plan revision, and evidence set.
- [ ] The report includes target accounting, commands, evidence, failures, unresolved work, elapsed time, cost, and interventions.
- [ ] The MVP performs no remote push, pull-request update, or merge.

## Artifact-record contract (folded from ravel-6pv)

- [ ] Branch, bundle, and report evidence are referenced from authoritative history only
  through the canonical scoped-v2 artifact-reference event, reusing the same record type
  as ravel-amn.6 and ravel-85q.2 — no second artifact record type.
- [ ] The review-bundle path is covered by tests proving publication/replay agreement and
  fail-closed rejection of malformed, unpublished, unsupported, or wrong-scope references
  before the scope head advances.
- [ ] Replay rebuilds the report's artifact metadata deterministically; frozen v1
  conversion behavior and `tests/wire.rs` fixtures are unchanged.
notes: Folded from ravel-6pv (closed, superseded): scoped-v2 must own the artifact record it admits. The FIRST of ravel-85q.2 / ravel-amn.6 / ravel-e1n.5 to land defines the ONE canonical artifact-reference payload type (registered in payload_type_registered, built on ArtifactRef/PublishedArtifact); the others reuse it and must not fork a second artifact record type.

title: Fold target accounting into trusted discovery
description:
## Disposition

Folded into `ravel-e1n.2`. Target identity, final rediscovery, accounting, and stop conditions form one invariant and should have one owner.
close_reason: Merged into trusted discovery so target identity, rediscovery, accounting, and stop conditions have one owner.

title: Implement the selected provider transport boundary
description:
## Outcome

Implement the closed transport boundary for the one selected MVP provider.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The adapter accepts a typed request and returns a small typed outcome set.
- [ ] The provider, model profile, request digest, token cap, timeout, and retry policy are explicit.
- [ ] SDK retries are disabled or proven to preserve the same operation identity and bounds.
- [ ] Secrets and provider-specific response objects do not enter durable domain records.
- [ ] A fake transport covers success, refusal, rate limit, timeout, transport failure, and malformed response.
design:
ravel-85q.1 plan. Rulings that bind it (bd memories): e06-provider-transport-dependency (add aws-sdk-bedrockruntime pinned), e06-provider-transport-dependency-pin-evidence (=1.139.0 verified: +1 lock entry, zero aws-smithy churn), e06-transport-token-cap (per-request cap only, no budget substrate), e06-bedrock-invocation-operation (non-streaming Converse, amending the panel's InvokeModel clause on new evidence), e06-transport-signoff-conditions (the six accepted sign-off corrections), e06-bedrock-sdk-facts (verified SDK surface).

Module placement: ONE new file src/provider.rs, declared `pub mod provider;` in src/lib.rs. Consistent with the crate's style for small modules (src/sync.rs is 29 lines, src/distributed.rs is 5) and with there being exactly one provider. A second provider becomes a variant of the same closed enum, not a new module.

U1 -- typed request and profile. ModelProvider closed enum with the single Bedrock variant and no `_` wildcard match anywhere, so a second provider breaks the build. ModelProfile pins provider, model_id, a configuration identifier, max_output_tokens: NonZeroU32, and any pinned temperature/top_p/stop_sequences; it exposes a configuration digest over its canonical form. InvocationRequest carries the profile, system text, prompt text and the stable operation id, and exposes a request digest over the adapter's OWN canonical serialization -- never SDK wire bytes, never Debug output (Debug on the SDK request types does not redact the text, and on InvokeModel it redacts body so a Debug digest would be constant across distinct prompts). The digest identifies an invocation; it does not reproduce the wire frame, so it survives SDK upgrades.

U2 -- transport. BedrockTransport::new(region, builder) copies configured() from src/storage/s3.rs:446 verbatim in policy: RetryConfig::disabled(), TimeoutConfig operation+attempt timeouts, StalledStreamProtectionConfig::enabled(), behavior_version_latest(), all applied AFTER the caller's builder. invoke() marks dispatch evidence BEFORE the await. No tokio::time anywhere in the module; bounds come from TimeoutConfig. Reuses storage::s3::AttemptHistory rather than adding a parallel type, passing the stable operation id where it expects an identity, with its doc generalized from 'one object key' to 'one logical operation identity'.

U3 -- outcomes. A small closed outcome set. Completed carries owned text, a crate-owned terminal reason mapped from StopReason, the provider request id, and Option<ReportedUse>; usage absent on a success response is reported-use-unavailable, a completed invocation with unknown usage, NOT malformed and NOT zero. Refusal maps from ContentFiltered/GuardrailIntervened. RateLimited maps from the typed ThrottlingException; ServiceQuotaExceededException, ServiceUnavailableException and ModelNotReadyException are each classified deliberately, never by a wildcard arm. Timeout, transport failure, malformed response and unknown follow the s3.rs discipline: only a pre-dispatch rejection and a construction failure on clean history prove no send. Nothing from aws_sdk_bedrockruntime crosses the boundary: no Message, ContentBlock, SystemContentBlock, TokenUsage, StopReason or SDK error type in an outcome or a durable record, and the module never Debug-prints or logs any of them.

U4 -- pre-dispatch cap validation. AC2's 'model profile permitted range' has no referent in the codebase, so the range source is a const table in this module keyed by model id. A cap outside it is refused before send with the proven-not-sent outcome.

U5 -- fake transport, AC5's six cases. No hand-written fake type: the SDK is driven through aws-smithy-runtime test-util StaticReplayClient and NeverClient exactly as src/storage/s3.rs test_support does, so there is no parallel implementation to drift. Cases: success (EndTurn), refusal (ContentFiltered), rate limit (429 WITH the x-amzn-errortype: ThrottlingException header, because variant resolution goes through generic.code() and a bare 429 deserializes to Unhandled -- a test without the header proves the opposite of its claim), timeout (NeverClient plus the attempt timeout), transport failure, malformed response. Plus the bare-429-lands-in-Unhandled case, and an AC3 test proving one retryable response yields exactly one recorded request.

Non-goals: campaign or grant budget enforcement (ravel-85q.4); manifests and traces (ravel-85q.2); ConverseStream, InvokeModel, tool_config, guardrail_config, additional_model_request_fields; any dyn provider trait, provider registry or profile registry.

Gates: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked. Note cargo check --locked fails on the first run after adding the dependency until the lock is regenerated with a plain cargo check.
notes:
stage=review-1 converged, commits 0f8a00c (implementation) and 6d3e706 (fixes). Five parallel reviewers. rust-code-reviewer 11 findings (3 blocking), invariant-test-review 9 (3 blocking) after running 12 mutation probes, test-strategy 4 (2 blocking), less-code 5 (2 blocking, 1 disputed), reduce-complexity 5 (2 blocking). PROCESS ERROR I MADE: I told reviewers they could mutate files with cp-restore and simultaneously ran my own mutation probes on src/provider.rs, so two writers shared one file. Both heavy reviewers detected it (one saw a probe test it never wrote, one saw guard lines vanish and reappear) and both re-ran against the pristine blob. My own two transposition probes from that window are invalid and I discarded them; theirs were re-verified. Serialize mutation work in future rounds. THE HEADLINE RESULT: 8 of 12 mutations deleted production logic and left the suite green. Two of the behaviors that passed were actually WRONG, not merely untested. (1) BLOCKING, evidence loss: classify computed reason, reported_use and provider_request_id then discarded all three whenever completion_text returned None, and marked the attempt possibly-sent where the provider had answered. A model_context_window_exceeded verdict arrives on a 200 with no text and 900k reported input tokens, so it was reported as an unreadable frame with the billing evidence thrown away, and TerminalReason::ContextWindowExceeded was near-unreachable. This is the exact failure mode the previous commit cited as the reason to prefer Converse over InvokeModel, reintroduced one layer up. Fixed by deciding the outcome from the stop reason before the text: is_refusal became precludes_completion covering ContentFiltered, GuardrailIntervened, ContextWindowExceeded and ModelOutputMalformed, all landing in Refused with reason plus usage plus request id. (2) BLOCKING, invariant: the clearing arms discarded prior_unknown unconditionally, so a verdict about attempt N cleared attempt N-1's possible billable work, and my comment claiming the update 'can over-report uncertainty and never under-report it' was false. An invocation has no remote state to reconcile, unlike S3 where a definite result resolves the object state. Fixed so the prior value always carries forward; S3 keeps clearing and the difference is documented on the shared type. (3) BLOCKING: no test produced a transport failure, and my commit message had falsely claimed the fake transport covered it. Fixed with a refused loopback connect to 127.0.0.1:1, which needs no new dependency and no network. Also fixed: the mark-and-resolve protocol moved onto AttemptHistory (its field is private again) rather than remaining a convention duplicated across two modules; InvocationRequest and InvocationOutcome got hand-written Debug over lengths and digests, because the module doc claimed owned domain types kept prompt and completion text out of logs and they did not; operation_id got its own error category, a length bound and documentation; the absent-probability digest marker became a presence byte instead of a reserved value; five uncalled accessors deleted; two rustdoc links to private consts fixed by making the documented bounds pub. REJECTED: less-code F1 asked to delete temperature/top_p/stop_sequences, auto-rejected citing e06-bedrock-invocation-operation whose binding consequences state the fixed profile IS max_tokens plus those pinned knobs, and mvp-outline section 13 which requires an exact fixed model configuration digest. reduce-complexity F1 asked to replace ReportedUse with a tuple; kept, because a named struct over three same-typed counts prevents exactly the transposition class the same reviewer flagged elsewhere. less-code F3/F4 asked to inline configuration_digest and the absorb helpers; kept, configuration_digest is required public API per AC2 and section 13, and absorb has ten call sites. VERIFICATION: all eight previously-vacuous mutations now fail. Gates green, 190 lib tests (was 181) plus 2/5/12 integration, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, only rustdoc warning is pre-existing at src/sync/head.rs:141. Incidental finding worth carrying forward: 900/1000 has no exact f32, so a pinned top_p of 900 reaches the wire as 0.8999999761581421 while the digest covers the exact thousandths -- which is why the profile stores thousandths.
stage=review-2 converged, commit 042dba7. Re-review by the three reviewers that raised blocking findings: test-strategy CLEAN (all 4 resolved), rust-code-reviewer CLEAN (all 11 resolved, 7 new non-blocking, and it correctly declined to revert my in-flight working-tree edit), invariant-test-review NOT CLEAN with 2 new blocking (F10 Debug redaction unguarded, F12 operation_id length bound untested) -- BOTH were already fixed in my working tree before its report arrived, and both are mutation-verified. Round-2 fixes: (a) rust N1, the residual of round 1's main defect -- my fix covered only the four MODELLED reasons, so an unmodelled stop reason with an empty content list still collapsed to a fieldless MalformedResponse and would lose billed input tokens exactly as the context-window case did; MalformedResponse now carries provider_request_id and reported_use so no response frame drops billing evidence whatever reasons the crate knows. (b) F11 answered by experiment the read-only reviewer could not run: dropping credentials_provider yields Unknown, NOT ConstructionFailure, so ProvenNotSent is unreachable through this boundary on both legs; that is now stated on the variant instead of implied covered. (c) Four guards over deletable logic, each mutation-verified: provider_request_id (the previous commit claimed to preserve it and no test read it -- replacing the call with None was green), both text bounds and the identity bound pinned at exactly the limit so > cannot drift to >=, and MalformedToolUse whose shared match arm is what makes it a verdict rather than a completion. (d) Two doc claims of mine wider than the code: precludes_completion said each of its reasons arrives with no assistant text, contradicted by this module's own test feeding text to a content filter; may_have_been_sent read as a claim about dispatch when a definite verdict clears it, so false means no unresolved uncertainty rather than no dispatch. Accepted without action: rust N6 (Debug hashes twice per format, bounded and only paid when something formats -- reduced from three to two passes), rust N7 / invariant F14 (the loopback test honors HTTP_PROXY so under a proxy the assertion holds by another path; ConnectorError is not reachable without adding aws-smithy-runtime-api as a dev-dependency, which the no-new-dependency rule forbids without a ruling, so the caveat is documented in the test instead), invariant F14 (one_history_cannot_span_two_provider_operations is cfg(debug_assertions) so bind is unguarded under --release). PROCESS: my batched python edit scripts aborted twice on a failed substitution and silently discarded the earlier edits in the same script; the mutation probes caught it both times, the second time across three findings at once. Switched to writing after each substitution. Gates green: 192 lib tests, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.
stage=stage-2 complete (doc-rigor then ponytail-review), commit 8cd8681. doc-rigor: 9 findings, 4 blocking, ALL APPLIED. The sharpest was that commit 042dba7's own message claimed the ProvenNotSent unreachability was 'stated on the variant' when it was not -- that edit was in a batch that aborted partway and the variant doc was byte-identical to the commit that introduced it, so a reader of the source could not find what the message said had been written down. Third occurrence of the aborted-script failure mode and the first to make a commit message false. Also blocking: MalformedResponse claimed to keep whatever evidence arrived while two of its three legs hardcoded both fields absent -- fixed in CODE rather than by weakening the doc, since RequestId for SdkError makes the request id available on both legs (one leg mutation-verified; the other is unreachable through these fakes because a decode failure arrives as ServiceError(Unhandled) on a 2xx, which is what round 1 discovered, and that is now documented on the arm); the InvocationOutcome enum doc said no variant asserts the provider did no work, contradicting ProvenNotSent thirty lines below and the module doc above; and the completion byte bound was justified by inferring that exceeding it means the provider ignored the cap, which does not follow because MAX_OUTPUT_TOKEN_CEILING is i32::MAX so a high-pinned profile produces honest completions past the bound -- it is a retention limit, not an inference. Non-blocking applied: malformed response was grouped with failures that 'leave the outcome unknown' when it is deliberately a separate verdict and what those cases share is leaving dispatch uncertainty in place; 'no provider type crosses this boundary' ignored the two SDK types in BedrockTransport::new's signature; the thousandths rationale blamed f32 for a formatting problem when to_bits is portable and the real reasons are one byte form per value and no duplicate bit patterns for one configuration; the Debug redaction list was closed with 'only' and missed guardrail image and trace fields; and a test doc narrated this branch's own history, which the repo comment rules exclude. ponytail-review: 6 findings, ALL REJECTED with reasons. F1 claimed ~160 lines of dead pub surface; its premise is factually wrong -- as_str, model_id(), configuration_digest, operation_id(), output_token_ceiling and the ProfileError Display/Error impls all have production callers inside the module, and every error type in this crate carries Display plus Error (sync.rs, db/worker.rs, domain/proposal.rs, domain/validation.rs, sync/event.rs, sync/replay.rs, db/projections.rs), so deleting them would break that convention. Only request_digest() and ReportedUse's three getters are test-only today, and those are exactly AC2's 'request digest ... explicit' and mvp-outline section 13's reported token use, whose consumer is ravel-85q.2. The real question F1 gestures at is pub versus pub(crate), not deletion, and nothing outside the crate can consume any of it; churning visibility now to re-widen when 85q.2 lands is the accretive pattern the repo guidance warns against, so it is deferred until that task shows what it needs. F2 asked to implement no Debug at all (stronger than redacting): rejected because assert_eq! on InvocationOutcome requires Debug for its failure message, so ~15 tests would lose all diagnostics and be forced to matches! with no output on failure. F3 asked to delete ProvenNotSent and map both legs to Unknown: rejected because the two have different evidence semantics -- ProvenNotSent carries the prior value forward while Unknown adds uncertainty, so the swap would assert possible dispatch for a request that was never constructed. F4 asked to merge two already-parameterized tests: rejected because they assert different outcomes (RateLimited versus Unknown). F5 doc compression: taste, and the reviewer called 21 lines for the file not egregious. F6 asked to delete the BedrockTransport struct for a free function: rejected on the reviewer's own reasoning, since it would weaken AC3 from proven-by-construction to a documented requirement.
close_reason: Bounded Bedrock transport landed behind a closed enum, dispatching non-streaming Converse. All five AC met: typed request and outcome set, explicit provider/profile/digest/cap/timeout/retry, retries disabled and proven by two tests that supply conflicting caller policy, no provider type in a request or outcome and no text reachable through Debug, and all six fake-transport cases covered. Five commits on task/ravel-85q.1, four gates green, six e06-* rulings recorded, two review rounds plus doc-rigor and ponytail-review converged.

title: Record immutable invocation manifests and traces
description:
## Outcome

Record immutable model invocation manifests and terminal traces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The manifest binds scope, plan digest, work revision, claim fence, `EffectGrant`, provider profile, prompt/input digests, and limits.
- [ ] Terminal traces distinguish success, refusal, timeout, canceled, definite failure, and unknown outcome.
- [ ] Usage and cost are recorded from provider evidence without trusting candidate text.
- [ ] Retries create new attempts and never overwrite prior records.
- [ ] Stored output and diagnostics are bounded and redacted.

## Artifact-record contract (folded from ravel-6pv)

- [ ] Manifest and trace records enter authoritative history only through the canonical
  scoped-v2 artifact-reference event, minted from a verified publication witness
  (`PublishedArtifact` in `src/storage/artifacts.rs`, metadata `ArtifactRef` in
  `src/domain/artifact.rs`).
- [ ] Publication and replay agree on the exact supported artifact record type; replay
  rebuilds manifest and trace metadata deterministically instead of trusting local state.
- [ ] Malformed, unpublished, unsupported, or wrong-scope artifact references fail before
  the scope head advances, with a negative test per rejection class.
- [ ] Frozen v1 conversion behavior and `tests/wire.rs` fixtures are unchanged.
design:
ravel-85q.2 implementation, commit fa0162d. Bound by e06-artifact-ref-event (the always-judged ruling, synthesized from a 4-option framing, a 3-judge panel and two sign-offs), plus e06-85q2-substrate-gotchas and e06-85q2-plan-admitted-precedent.

WHAT LANDED. New payload type artifact_reference in src/scope.rs: ArtifactKind closed enum (InvocationManifest, InvocationTrace) parsed from fixed lowercase strings with an unknown string refused as WireError::InvalidValue; ArtifactReferencePayload carrying kind, the full ArtifactRef, work_id, work_revision, grant_digest and attempt, with size and creation_time_unix_ms bounded in the constructor because ArtifactRef accepts any u64 by design; ArtifactReferenceEvent refusing sequence < 2; WireArtifactReferencePayload with a frozen field set and declaration order; the encode/decode pair with the canonicality re-encode check. Registered at all four points: scope::payload_type_registered, sync::event::validate_registered, db::projections::ScopeProjectionPayload plus its fold arm, sync::replay::typed_payload.

THE FOLD writes nothing and resolves via ARTIFACT_REFERENCE_RESOLVABLE_SQL, two EXISTS predicates both monotone in the applied prefix: an admitted_work row by (scope_id, work_id, work_revision), and an applied_scope_events row by (scope_id, payload_type='grant_activated', grant_digest). Neither is keyed on operation_id, because the reference is appended under its own operation rather than the activation's.

NEW MODULE src/invocation.rs: InvocationBinding (scope, plan digest, work revision, claim fence, grant, attempt -- AC1's bindings, carried by both records so each stands alone); InvocationManifest taking a &ModelProfile so the record names the profile the transport actually used rather than restating its parts; InvocationTrace with TerminalOutcome, a closed six-value enum including Canceled which the transport has no equivalent for; BoundedText retaining a prefix beside the full length and address, so AC5's bounding is retention rather than refusal and text no one wants durable is absent by construction; content-addressed stored_bytes plus decode_manifest/decode_trace that re-encode and refuse bytes not reproducing themselves, which is what makes publication and replay agree (AC7).

APPEND PATH src/sync/head.rs::append_artifact_reference with the witness gate: it takes an ArtifactAdmission carrying the &PublishedArtifact that publish returned and refuses a witness whose namespace is not the store's, before any dispatch. Scope is derived from the fenced parent so a caller cannot pass two scopes that disagree. Carries cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code)) because its production caller lands with the task owning invocation orchestration; expect flags the attribute for removal once that exists.

TESTS, each mutation-verified where noted. Codec round-trip pinning ARTIFACT_REFERENCE_EVENT_DIGEST with pairwise-distinct values for the two adjacent identity strings and two adjacent bounded integers, so a transposition in the frozen order cannot round-trip unnoticed. Unmodelled record kind refused. All eight integer bindings bounded on both sides. Fold resolution: admitted plus activated passes and writes no work columns; unadmitted revision, unknown work id, and a grant with no activation event each refused with the cursor unmoved. Monotonicity test: an earlier grant stays resolvable after a later activation moves admitted_work's grant columns, and clearing claim_fence to NULL leaves a reference admissible, which is what keeps a fresh rebuild from refusing its own history. Replay routing test proving an artifact suffix reaches its fold rather than the unsupported arm -- mutation-verified by deleting the conversion arm. Witness gate refused before any dispatch -- mutation-verified by deleting the namespace check. Registration distinction pinned: 'artifact' stays unregistered so the existing negative test survives while 'artifact_reference' is registered. Seven invocation record tests: manifest and trace round-trips with digest-mismatch, missing-prefix, trailing-byte and cross-type rejections; absent usage versus usage of zero distinct in both bytes and address; every terminal outcome round-tripping; output retained to the bound with the whole addressed and a multi-byte character dropped whole; every record rejection; and a record past the canonical cap refused.

AC9 NOTE for the PR: its first half has no referent. The v1 converter it names (CampaignCreated/WorkflowStarted/ArtifactPublished/ConversionError/SchedulingEffect) is absent from src/ entirely, removed by the scoped-v2 realignment, so only 'fixtures unchanged' is checkable and that is verified. This must be stated, not claimed as fully met.

STILL OPEN: no production caller publishes a manifest or trace and appends its reference; that orchestration belongs to the task that owns invocation lifecycle. AC6's mint path exists and is gated; nothing yet drives it.

Gates green at fa0162d: fmt, check --locked, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, test --locked with 205 lib plus 2/5/12 integration. tests/fixtures byte-unchanged.
notes: Folded from ravel-6pv (closed, superseded): scoped-v2 must own the artifact record it admits. The FIRST of ravel-85q.2 / ravel-amn.6 / ravel-e1n.5 to land defines the ONE canonical artifact-reference payload type (registered in payload_type_registered, built on ArtifactRef/PublishedArtifact); the others reuse it and must not fork a second artifact record type.

title: Own provider cancellation and unknown outcomes
description:
## Outcome

Own provider-call cancellation, unknown-outcome reconciliation, and shutdown.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No call starts without the current claim and grant.
- [ ] Per-call and campaign-wide concurrency, deadline, token, attempt, and spend limits are enforced before send.

title: Build one bounded model-provider execution path
description:
## Outcome

Build one bounded model-provider execution path used by the Change MVP.

## Scope

One selected provider and model profile. The substrate records exact inputs, authority, limits, terminal outcome, and unknown-outcome reconciliation. Research roles and a second provider are post-signal work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An admitted Change action can execute through one closed provider adapter.
- [ ] Calls are bounded by time, tokens, attempts, parallelism, and campaign budget.
- [ ] Every call has an immutable manifest and terminal trace bound to current authority.
- [ ] Cancellation and ambiguous outcomes do not double-spend or silently repeat work.
notes:
Completed input: E02's conservative definite/unknown outcome pattern and immutable content publication. Provider-specific bytes stay behind a new closed adapter.
E06 autonomous run playbook (plan: while-we-finish-up-glimmering-hopcroft): order ravel-yno -> ravel-85q.1 -> ravel-85q.2 -> ravel-1rc -> ravel-85q.4. Stacked PRs: each task branch based on previous task branch, yno on main. Worktrees at ravel-wt/<suffix>. Per task: claim, plan (plan-forge, persist via --design), scope-guard vs AC, implement, review round 1 (rust-code-reviewer, less-code, reduce-complexity, invariant-test-review, test-strategy in parallel), converge (blocking findings all fixed; non-blocking fixed unless >~20 lines churn or AC conflict; disputed -> judge panel), stage 2 (doc-rigor then ponytail-review), gates (cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked), bd export on task branch, push + gh pr create --base PREV, close + advance. Design questions (mandatory route, never unilateral): new public API/module boundary, payload_type_registered() changes, SQL schema change, frozen v1 conversion or tests/wire.rs fixtures, AC term with no substrate, cross-task contracts, new dependencies. Rulings stored as bd memories keyed e06-*. Round cap 3 then judge panel. Failure: 3 failed attempts -> expert consult -> bd human + STOP (chain strictly sequential).

title: Run one distributed Change campaign
description:
## Outcome

Turn one bounded code-change objective into a trusted, reviewable result using two workers.

## MVP flow

Trusted discovery -> admitted target groups -> concurrent candidates -> deterministic evaluation -> bounded selection -> final target accounting -> local branch, bundle, and report.

The user reviews and performs any external merge. Remote PR automation and recursive workers are post-signal work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All work and retries enter through root `PlanRevision` admission.
- [ ] Two workers execute against the same exact base with separate claims and grants.
- [ ] Every target ends resolved, rejected, blocked, or unresolved.
- [ ] Final trusted rediscovery finds no unclassified target.
- [ ] The result can be reconstructed and reviewed without access to worker state.

title: Bind grant recording and the reserved-budget sum to the row's admitting plan
description:
## Context

Found by the rust-code-reviewer lane during ravel-5d2.1 (which added admitted_work.plan_digest and made scheduling select rows bound to scopes.active_plan_digest).

RECORD_GRANT_SQL ends with EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM scopes WHERE scope_id = ?1 AND active_plan_digest = ?5 AND scope_epoch <= ?8). That proves the issuing IDENTITY names the scope active plan. It says nothing about the row: admitted_work.plan_digest is not compared. So a grant can be recorded against a revision a superseded plan admitted — consuming an attempt slot and drawing reserved units on a row continuable_work will never return.

The same statement sums sibling granted_units across every revision of the scope regardless of admitting plan, so units drawn by a now-superseded revision keep charging against reserved_budget_units.

## Why it is not urgent

Unreachable today: ADMIT_PLAN_SQL still refuses a second plan, so every row in a scope carries one plan digest. This becomes live the moment plan supersession is implemented.

## Desired state

- RECORD_GRANT_SQL requires the row plan_digest to be the scope active_plan_digest (or explicitly documents why the identity check alone is sufficient).
- The reserved-budget sibling sum is scoped to the plan whose reservation it is charging, or the reservation is explicitly defined as spanning plans.
- A test pins whichever semantics is chosen, using the direct-write supersession fixture ravel-5d2.1 added (supersede_plan test helper).

## Note

ravel-5d2.1 deliberately left this alone (spec sections 4.3 and 6): the change there was scheduling-read scoped, and widening a grant-authority statement without the supersession mechanism to test against would have been speculative.

title: Bind lease_until into the sealed claim and submission wire records
description:
`docs/mvp-outline.md` 9.1 lists `lease_until` among the bindings of *every* claim and sealed submission, and requires intake to accept a seal only when "every binding agrees". `WireClaimState::Sealed` (src/distributed/claims.rs) carries only the submission artifact, so a sealed claim and its submission record drop the lease generation they completed under, and `intake` cannot compare it.

Scope: add the field to `ScopeClaimState::Sealed` and `SealedSubmission`, encode/decode it in both records, and extend the claim-vs-submission agreement check in `intake`.

Explicitly out of scope: rejecting a completion because its lease had expired. 9.2 resolves the late-submit race through fence supersession plus the shared-ETag CAS between reclamation and completion, and 9.1 states an unexpired claim stays valid across controller takeover. A wall-clock rejection would discard a legitimately completed result nobody reclaimed and would make acceptance depend on worker clocks.

Raised as a P2 on PR 42 (comment 3781672523); deferred there because it changes two public record schemas rather than one call site.

title: Seal one E10 preflight receipt and execution schedule
description:
## Context

E10 runs the precommitted MVP feasibility experiment, so every execution input and validity rule must be fixed before the first result is visible. This task creates the minimum receipt needed to prove that the frozen Research and Change comparisons use their exact sealed contracts and that the eventual decision cannot drift after observation.

The receipt is not a new experiment framework. It is a compact set of immutable references plus the concrete execution schedule for both MVP campaigns.

## Current State

The repository currently contains `docs/epics.md`, `docs/mvp-outline.md`, and beads metadata; it has no code or experiment artifacts. E01 is expected to produce the checked-in private pilot/precommit configuration. Frozen E01-E04 supply unchanged v1 proof artifacts. V2-P1, E05, V2-P3, and E06-E09 supply scoped chains/projections, separate claim/scope fencing, admitted plans, grants, escrow, certificates, settlement, Research, candidate, evaluator/process/provider/code-host, and Change artifacts and tests.

E10's contract is in `docs/epics.md` under “E10 — Run the Precommitted MVP Feasibility Gate”. Treatment shapes and measurements are in `docs/mvp-outline.md` §32; hard invariants and MVP completion rules are in §43 and §44.

## Desired State

One small, immutable preflight receipt references the authoritative E01 Git revision/content digests and the existing E02-E09 artifact, run, and owning-test identities. It validates the E01-frozen schedule, capture, timing, validity, and replacement rules (ravel-j4t) by revision/digest and seals only what E01 leaves open — concrete host identities, A/B/C host allocation, execution order, and the deterministic schedule-seed instantiation — before any E10 observation, without copying those artifacts into new manifests or inventories. E10 does not author or reseal timing, validity, replacement, or schedule rules after the E06/E09 live runs.

The receipt binds the scoped-v2 campaign/scope/plan/grant/certificate/settlement evidence contracts without inventing unresolved payload schemas.

The receipt has an objective `READY` or `BLOCKED` result. A missing or mismatched required input cannot be replaced by operator choice.

## Implementation Guidance

- Follow the private experiment configuration/output convention established by E01. Do not introduce a public schema, migration system, experiment framework, or runtime module solely for this receipt.
- Reference E01 values by revision/digest rather than duplicating the Research question, Change repository/base/discovery rule, treatment definitions, bounds, run counts, provider models and exact fixed model configurations, evaluator commands, branch policy, scoring rules, or success criteria.
- Reference the immutable outputs and owning-test artifacts produced by E02-E09.
- Validate the E01-frozen treatment-application unit, analysis unit, reset/interference rules, timing boundaries, faulted-run placement, invalid-attempt validity/replacement rules, and treatment-neutral capture contract by revision/digest; seal only the E10-owned instantiation: A/B/C host allocation, execution order, and deterministic schedule seed. Record which reserved upstream treatment-C observations (qualifying `ravel-85q.8` / `ravel-e1n.7` runs) are consumed.
- Record at least three independent host identities and capabilities, required measurement captureability, and the existing fault hooks needed for distributed and composed-failure runs.
- Define separate fields for attempt status, evidence-validity verdict, and treatment outcome. Treatment outcome is populated only for evidence-valid attempts. Retain every attempt and seal the rule for counting or replacing invalid attempts.
- Seal this transition table: blocked preflight or invalid/incomplete execution yields no go/no-go and denies MVP completion; a valid `NO-GO` completes E10 but denies MVP completion; a valid `GO` completes E10 but permits MVP completion only when every mandatory gate is `PASS`.
- If allocation/order/reset/interference evidence cannot support a treatment-effect claim, require the final report to mark that question `INDETERMINATE`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The receipt resolves the exact E01 input revision and content digests for both frozen comparison campaigns, all three treatments, frozen bounds/run counts, scoring rules, and success criteria. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] The receipt references the E01-frozen treatment-application/analysis units, reset/interference rules, timing boundaries, fault placement, and validity/replacement rules by revision/digest — authoring or resealing none of them — and records host allocation, execution order, and schedule seed before the first observation. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] At least three independent hosts and all required distributed capabilities pass preflight. (E10 AC2)
- [ ] Captureability is proven for every mandatory Research and Change measurement; a missing required field produces `BLOCKED`. (E10 AC4, AC5)
- [ ] Existing frozen-v1 and scoped-v2 artifact/run/owning-test identities are referenced without copying them into a second evidence inventory. (E10 AC7)
- [ ] Attempt status, evidence validity, and treatment outcome are distinct, every attempt is retained, and the invalid-attempt counting/replacement rule is the E01-frozen rule, validated rather than defined here. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] Reserved upstream treatment-C observations (qualifying `ravel-85q.8` / `ravel-e1n.7` runs executed under the frozen capture contract) are validated and recorded as consumed C observations exactly once. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] The blocked/invalid/valid-no-go/valid-go/MVP-completion transition table is recorded exactly and cannot be edited after observation. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] Any missing or mismatched required precommit field, host capability, captureability check, or mandatory upstream identity yields `BLOCKED`; no substitute can be selected by an operator. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] No experiment framework, public configuration API, telemetry service, proof registry, or final evidence manifest is introduced. (E10 AC8 and explicit prohibitions)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit/fixture:** Use a minimal valid receipt fixture plus missing/digest-mismatch cases; verify deterministic schedule generation from the recorded seed and fail-closed validation.
- **Integration:** Resolve real E01 and E02-E09 references, probe all three hosts, and verify required record fields and fault hooks are observable without running treatments.
- **Manual review:** Confirm that the receipt contains references rather than copied definitions, was sealed before observations, and has no operator-selectable fallback.

## Design Gate
Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §0, §43, §32, §33, §44; decomposed from epic ravel-4dw via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e10-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

## Final Step

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.
notes: Post-signal controlled feasibility work. This preserves the frozen E01 A/B/C experiment contract and its reserved run IDs. The active product-validation trial is tracked separately under ravel-pmf.

title: Execute the frozen Research treatment matrix
description:
## Context

E10 must compare the frozen Research treatments: one strong agent on one machine, multiple agents on one machine, and the distributed campaign. This task runs that matrix exactly as sealed and retains enough evidence to measure results and prove real autonomous multi-machine behavior.

The task exercises the Research pilot built by E06; it does not add Research workflow behavior or redefine the experiment.

## Current State

title: Run the composed external-unknown-outcome recovery scenario
description:
## Context

E02-E09 prove individual durability, fencing, workflow, provider, process, evaluator, and code-host boundaries. E10 needs one final live scenario showing that those existing mechanisms compose when an active worker and parent or child scoped controller fail around an external call whose result is unknown.

This is a bounded proof of the selected scenario, not a generic fault-injection or recovery framework.

## Current State

The repository currently has only design documents and beads metadata. By the time this task runs, prior epics must supply the scope chains, separate claim/scope fencing, fresh scope-selective SQLite reconstruction, admitted plans, grants, certificates, settlement, operation identities, provider/code-host reconciliation, process cleanup, and workflow terminal-state machinery. Steps 2 and 3 must have completed the live pilot matrices on the preflighted hosts.

E10 AC3 defines the composed scenario. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §43 forbids unfenced completion, stale-controller commits, unreconciled side effects, exactly-once claims, and unbounded action chains; §44 requires real failover and no duplicate authoritative effect, idempotent child settlement where applicable, and conserved escrow.

## Desired State

One valid, ordered, immutable three-host scenario trace proves that the selected external call crossed its boundary and lost its response, the active worker and controller were killed at the registered points, recovery reconstructed from the exact fresh selected `ScopeHead` and active plan lineage on another host, and stale `claim_fence` and stale `scope_epoch` authority could not publish after takeover.

Recovery ends within frozen bounds in one coherent verifier-bounded completion or explicit `UNRESOLVED`, with child certificate handling, idempotent settlement, conserved escrow, and quarantined unknown reserve preserved. The scenario leaves the environment restored, has no duplicate authoritative effect, settles any child idempotently, and conserves escrow.

## Implementation Guidance

- Reuse existing §42 modules and hooks, especially operation-local `recovery/reconcile.rs` (there is no generic `recovery/outbox.rs`; reconciliation stays operation-local), `sync/scope_head.rs`, `sync/replay.rs`, `distributed/claims.rs`, `distributed/fencing.rs`, `distributed/scope_controller.rs`, and `db/scope_projections.rs`.
- Before injection, record: target campaign/run and external operation identity; expected scope/plan/work/grant/worker/controller identities and separate `claim_fence`/`scope_epoch` values; no-fault baseline; an injection oracle independent of the worker/controller under test; blast-radius exclusions; abort guardrails; restoration/cleanup procedure; and explicit invalidation criteria.
- Invalidation includes wrong target, failure to inject, missing independent witness, recovery starting before proven response loss, protocol deviation, or guardrail breach. Retain an invalid attempt but do not count it as a failed treatment/scenario outcome.
- Prove with existing immutable records that the external request crossed the boundary and that its response was lost before recovery began. Do not infer this merely from local absence.
- Kill the active worker around the call, then kill the active controller while the outcome remains unknown. Recover or promote scoped authority on another host after fresh scope-selective SQLite reconstruction and exact fresh-`ScopeHead`/active-plan verification.
- Use the owning `EffectGrant`, stable operation identity, and complete selected-scope-chain/remote-state reconciliation path. Reintroduce delayed stale worker/controller activity and verify fence rejection.
- Enforce frozen attempt/depth/deadline/cost bounds, cleanup process groups/resources, and restore the test environment. Do not claim exactly-once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pre-registered target manifest identifies the campaign, external operation, scope/plan/work/grant/worker/controller identities and separate fences, hosts, injection points, and expected evidence. (E10 AC3)
- [ ] A no-fault baseline, independent injection oracle, blast-radius exclusions, abort guardrails, restoration path, and invalidation criteria are recorded before injection. (E10 AC3)
- [ ] Existing evidence independently proves the external call crossed the boundary and its response was lost before recovery started. (E10 AC3)
- [ ] On at least three independent hosts, the active worker and controller are killed at the registered points and recovery authority moves to another host. (E10 AC2, AC3)
- [ ] The replacement scoped controller reconstructs selected SQLite state from object storage and verifies the exact fresh `ScopeHead` and active plan lineage before authoritative action. (E10 AC2, AC3)
- [ ] Reconciliation uses operation identity plus complete selected-scope-chain/remote-state evidence; absence from one local view is not treated as failure. (E10 AC3)
- [ ] Delayed stale worker and scoped-controller actions are rejected separately by `claim_fence` and `scope_epoch`. (E10 AC3, AC10)
- [ ] Recovery remains within frozen bounds and ends in one coherent completion or explicit `UNRESOLVED`, with no duplicate authoritative effect and no exactly-once claim; any child settles idempotently and escrow remains conserved. (E10 AC3, AC10)
- [ ] Invalid attempts are retained and replaced/counted only under the Step 1 sealed rule. (E10 AC1, AC3)
- [ ] Cleanup/restoration completes and the final selected scope chains/root rollup and fresh projections agree on terminal state. (E10 AC3)

## Testing Strategy

- **Live baseline:** Run the same selected path without faults and retain its expected operation and terminal-state evidence.
- **Live fault integration:** Execute the registered worker/controller kills on real hosts and capture the independent oracle, immutable ordering, reconstruction, reconciliation, and stale-fence witnesses.
- **Validation:** Automatically reject a trace with a missed/wrong injection, missing boundary-crossing or response-loss proof, early recovery, guardrail violation, or inconsistent terminal state.
- **Manual review:** Verify blast radius, bounds, no exactly-once wording, environment restoration, and absence of duplicate authoritative effect.

## Design Gate

title: Implement the one offline renderer and score both MVP campaigns
description:
## Context

E10 needs comparable Research and Change measurements and a reproducible CSV/Markdown output, but the epic explicitly prohibits a telemetry product or general experiment framework. The smallest implementation is one offline renderer that is also the sole scoring and aggregation path.

This task converts retained immutable records into the two fixed tables required by the pilots. It does not change scoring rules or infer missing data.

## Current State

The repository currently has no code; by this task, E01 must provide the frozen scoring/outcome definitions and Steps 2-4 must provide retained Research, Change, and composed-scenario records. Frozen-v1 and scoped-v2 owning epics provide scope decisions/observations, provider usage, evaluator results, target/candidate identities, code-host records, and immutable traces.

Required measures are listed in E10 AC4/AC5 and `docs/mvp-outline.md` §32. E10 AC8 requires a small offline CSV/Markdown script and prohibits metrics services, dashboards, exporters, permanent baselines, adaptive reruns, and significance claims.

## Desired State

One small offline script reads the sealed receipt and retained records, applies only frozen E01 definitions, and emits deterministic CSV plus a Markdown report draft. It produces one fixed Research table and one fixed Change table, with provenance back to immutable identities.

The script is the only calculation path. Required missing data remains visible but causes a non-successful validation result and marks the affected criterion and experiment incomplete/invalid.

## Implementation Guidance

- Follow the E01 private experiment/output convention. The §42 runtime tree does not prescribe an E10 reporting module; do not add a daemon/runtime module, package, generic schema, plugin API, or service solely for this script.
- Read records from the existing durable/output formats. Do not create a second run index, evidence manifest, or independent aggregation/reconciliation implementation.
- Research table fields: run/treatment/validity identity, wall time, supported/incorrect/omitted/unresolved conclusions, useful evidence, discriminating follow-up, provider calls/tokens/usage/cost, duplicate work, scaling efficiency, and controller idle/bottleneck time.
- Change table fields: run/treatment/validity identity, correctly resolved targets, wall time, omissions, semantic corrections and candidate rejections, integration conflicts, wasted work, provider usage/cost per resolved target, worker utilization, scaling efficiency, and final rediscovery.
- Use E01's frozen denominators, timing boundaries, cost interpretation, and formulas. Include unfavorable valid treatment outcomes. List invalid attempts separately and apply only the sealed Step 1 count/replacement rule.
- Every aggregate must carry or resolve its source campaign/scope/plan/work/claim/grant/run/target/candidate/evaluator/code-host identities as applicable.
- Preserve an unavailable cell with its source-backed reason, but fail AC4/AC5 and mark the experiment incomplete/invalid for any required unavailable value. Never default, estimate, or drop it.
- Keep analysis descriptive. Do not add significance tests, confidence claims, causal claims, adaptive reruns, or result-dependent exclusions.
- Use a tiny smoke fixture and concise `--help`; do not add byte-for-byte CSV/Markdown golden snapshots or standalone usage documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One offline invocation emits CSV and a Markdown report draft from retained records, with deterministic row and heading order. (E10 AC8)
- [ ] The Research table contains every required AC4 measure plus provider invocation and scoped-controller idle/bottleneck fields needed by §32/AC9. (E10 AC4, AC9)
- [ ] The Change table contains every required AC5 measure and final trusted rediscovery. (E10 AC5)
- [ ] Frozen E01 definitions are the only source for scoring, denominators, timing, cost, duplicate/wasted-work, utilization, and scaling calculations. (E10 AC1, AC4, AC5)
- [ ] Every valid scheduled Research/Change run appears exactly once; invalid attempts remain separately visible and are not scored as treatment outcomes. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] Every aggregate traces to immutable campaign/scope/plan/work/claim/grant/run/target/candidate/evaluator/code-host identities as applicable. (E10 AC4, AC5)
- [ ] A required unavailable Research or Change value is retained with its reason, causes validation failure, fails AC4/AC5, and marks the experiment incomplete/invalid. (E10 AC4, AC5, AC10)
- [ ] A tiny fixture checks required rows, columns, headings, totals, identities, missing-field failure, and deterministic ordering through the same production calculation path. (E10 AC8)
- [ ] The script provides concise `--help` and adds no golden snapshots, separate aggregation implementation, standalone usage guide, service, dashboard, exporter, permanent baseline, adaptive rerun, or statistical-significance machinery. (E10 AC8)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit/fixture:** Run one tiny fixture through the real renderer and check required structure, known totals, identity propagation, ordering, duplicate-ID rejection, and missing-required-field failure.
- **Integration:** Run against the complete retained E10 record set; reconcile scheduled attempt identities, scope/plan/grant identities, target denominators, provider usage, evaluator results, and final rediscovery.
- **Manual review:** Trace representative rows and every headline aggregate to immutable sources; scan output and code for post-hoc exclusions, alternate calculations, significance/causal language, and prohibited infrastructure.

title: Adjudicate autonomy and owning-correctness evidence in the final report
description:
## Context

E10 must prove that routine pilot progress was autonomous and reference the correctness evidence owned by earlier epics. To keep the gate small, these statuses belong directly in the final Markdown report's single gate checklist rather than in a separate proof packet or registry.

This task performs the focused autonomy and owning-evidence adjudication before the final §43/§44 decision.

## Current State

The repository currently has no code. By this task, E02-E09 must have produced owning tests and immutable artifacts for durability, projection, fencing, provider/process/evaluator/code-host boundaries; Steps 2-4 must have retained work/decision records, operator actions, and composed-failure evidence; Step 5 must have created the Markdown report draft.

E10 AC6 defines forbidden routine human control. AC7 names correctness evidence for S3 ambiguity, SQLite projection, claim/controller fencing, provider unknown outcomes, process cleanup, trusted evaluation, and code-host reconciliation.

## Desired State

The final report draft contains one gate checklist with objective autonomy rows, the original eight correctness-mechanism rows, and the additive scoped-v2 rows. Each row references the owning test and existing immutable artifact identity; no mechanism is reimplemented and no assertion-level registry is created.

Routine human intervention produces `FAIL`, not an omission or explanatory waiver. Missing owning evidence produces `MISSING` and remains visible for the final MVP gate.

## Implementation Guidance

- Update the final Markdown report draft emitted by Step 5. Do not create a standalone autonomy matrix, correctness index, proof packet, CI catalog, or assertion registry.
- Adjudicate autonomy using immutable admitted plans/work, routing, immutable observations, scoped decisions, integration, certificates, settlement, and operator-action records from Steps 2-4.
- Allowed human inputs are objective/configuration or explicitly configured approval observations. Human output remains proposal basis and cannot bypass deterministic admission, mint grants, or override a scoped decision. Post-run grading is measurement only.
- Mark AC6 `FAIL` if humans assigned routine work, approved routine conclusions, chose ordinary candidates, performed routine safe-branch integration, or extended routine bounds.
- Enumerate the original eight correctness mechanisms separately and add scoped-v2 rows without merging the original proof obligations:
  1. S3 ambiguity.
  2. SQLite atomic projection.
  3. Claim fencing.
  4. Controller fencing (scoped-v2 scope authority; owned by `distributed/scope_controller.rs`).
  5. Provider unknown outcomes.
  6. Process cleanup.
  7. Trusted evaluation.
  8. Code-host reconciliation.
  9. Mixed-version rejection and independent scope replay.
  10. Scoped-v2 `claim_fence` ownership and submission rejection.
  11. Scoped-v2 `scope_epoch` decision rejection.
  12. Deterministic plan admission and typed proposal basis.
  13. `EffectGrant` enforcement and stable operation reconciliation.
  14. Delegation, certificate validation, idempotent settlement, escrow conservation, and quarantined unknown reserve.
- For each mechanism, reference the owning frozen-v1 or scoped-v2 epic test identity and its existing immutable artifact/run identity. Do not copy assertions or invent a new test in E10.
- Use only `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `MISSING`, with a short evidence reference/reason. Carry every non-pass state into Step 7.
- Relevant §42 ownership includes `storage/s3.rs`, `sync/`, `db/projections.rs` and `distributed/claims.rs` for the frozen-v1 record, `distributed/scope_controller.rs` for scoped controller fencing (`distributed/controller.rs` is not a completed E01-E04 proof), `distributed/fencing.rs`, `models/`, `sandbox/process.rs`, `oracle/`, `code_host/`, and `recovery/reconcile.rs`; E10 only references their evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The final report directly classifies whether humans supplied only objective/configuration/outer-boundary authority. (E10 AC6)
- [ ] Any routine human work assignment, conclusion approval, ordinary candidate choice, safe-branch integration, or bound extension is an explicit `FAIL`. (E10 AC6)
- [ ] Frozen-v1 claim fencing and scoped-v2 controller fencing remain separate original rows, preserving the original eight-mechanism count; scoped-v2 `claim_fence` and `scope_epoch` also remain separate, and additive admission/grant/certificate/settlement rows do not replace any original mechanism. (E10 AC7)
- [ ] Each original and additive row references its owning E02-E09 test and existing immutable artifact identity. (E10 AC7)
- [ ] No E10 substitute test, duplicated recovery mechanism, assertion-level registry, separate proof packet, or multi-matrix artifact is added. (E10 AC7 and explicit prohibitions)
- [ ] Every row uses `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `MISSING`, and every non-pass state is preserved for the final MVP-completion decision. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] References resolve to immutable artifacts and contain no secret material. (E10 AC7, AC10)

## Testing Strategy

- **Reference validation:** Resolve every owning-test and immutable-artifact identity and reject dangling, mutable, or duplicate references.
- **Fixture:** Use a tiny checklist fixture with one allowed human action, one forbidden routine action, and one missing artifact to prove `PASS`/`FAIL`/`MISSING` behavior.
- **Manual review:** Inspect operator records, scope histories, and root rollups for unrecorded routine authority and confirm all original and additive mechanisms are independently represented without copied assertions.

By this task, Step 5 must have emitted validated Research and Change tables, CSV, and a Markdown report draft; Step 6 must have populated autonomy plus original and additive owning-correctness rows. E02-E09 and Steps 2-4 must supply immutable evidence for hard invariants, campaign behavior, real multi-machine execution, failover, and composed recovery.

The gate is defined by E10 AC9/AC10, `docs/mvp-outline.md` §43's thirty-five invariants, and every §44 definition-of-done requirement across distributed substrate, autonomous control, Research, Change, failure behavior, and measurement.

## Desired State

The final Markdown report contains one complete gate checklist, validated fixed measurement tables, an explicit experiment-validity status, an evidence-backed `GO` or `NO-GO` only when the experiment is valid, an E10-completion status, and an MVP-completion status.

Every checklist row is `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `MISSING` with an immutable reference. Any mandatory non-pass state denies MVP completion. The final report answers only the questions required by E10 AC9.

## Implementation Guidance

- Complete the same checklist started in Step 6; do not create additional invariant, distributed-proof, or definition-of-done matrices.
- Enumerate all thirty-five §43 invariants, preserving every original row and adding the scoped-v2 rows. Map each to an owning E02-E09 artifact or direct E10 run/scenario evidence; never infer an invariant merely from a terminal campaign state.
- Enumerate every §44 bullet under:
  - distributed substrate,
  - autonomous control,
  - Research,
  - Change,
  - failure behavior,
  - measurement.
- A §44 row may reference existing owning-epic evidence. Any `FAIL` or `MISSING` row denies MVP completion.
- Apply the Step 1 sealed transition table without edits:
  - `BLOCKED` or invalid/incomplete execution: no go/no-go, E10 incomplete, MVP denied.
  - Valid completed experiment yielding frozen `NO-GO`: E10 complete, MVP denied.
  - Valid `GO` with any non-pass mandatory AC6/AC7/AC10, §43, or §44 row: E10 complete, MVP denied.
  - Valid `GO` with all mandatory rows `PASS`: E10 complete and MVP completion allowed.
- Answer only E10 AC9: where distribution helped, where scaling stopped, whether judge diversity and disagreement added value, what work was duplicated, and whether S3, scoped-controller, admission, settlement, or evaluator paths were bottlenecks.
- Mark a treatment-effect answer `INDETERMINATE` when host/time/provider allocation, order, reset, or interference evidence cannot support it. Do not fill gaps with causal claims.
- Do not add general finding-trustworthiness, controller-created-work value, code-host bottleneck, or strongest-workflow ranking sections.
- Publish final CSV and Markdown using stable evidence references. Do not add a separate evidence manifest, dashboard, service, significance calculation, or secret data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The final report contains every required Research and Change measurement; any required unavailable measure makes the experiment invalid/incomplete rather than merely caveated. (E10 AC4, AC5)
- [ ] The single gate checklist retains Step 6's autonomy and all original/additive correctness rows and adds every one of the thirty-five §43 invariants. (E10 AC6, AC7, AC10)
- [ ] The checklist maps every §44 definition-of-done bullet across distributed substrate, autonomous control, Research, Change, failure behavior, and measurement. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] Every mandatory row is `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `MISSING` with an immutable owning-epic or E10 reference; any `FAIL`/`MISSING` denies MVP completion. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] The report proves actual three-host execution, late join, worker loss, scoped-controller failover, remote roles, fresh reconstruction, stale-authority rejection, and composed external-outcome recovery or explicit unresolved state. (E10 AC2, AC3, AC10)
- [ ] `GO` or `NO-GO` is issued only for a valid completed experiment and follows the frozen E01 criteria without reruns, exclusions, or threshold changes. (E10 AC9, AC10)
- [ ] A valid `NO-GO` is marked as completed E10 work but cannot mark the MVP complete. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] A valid `GO` marks the MVP complete only when every mandatory AC6/AC7/AC10 row, all 35 §43 rows, and every §44 row is `PASS`. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] The report answers only the AC9 scaling, judge-diversity/disagreement, duplication, and S3/scoped-controller/admission/settlement/evaluator bottleneck questions; unsupported effects are `INDETERMINATE`. (E10 AC9)
- [ ] Final CSV/Markdown aggregates trace to immutable records, contain no secrets, and include no significance/confidence/unsupported causal claim or prohibited telemetry/framework artifact. (E10 AC8, AC9)

## Testing Strategy

- **Automated validation:** Reject missing checklist rows, unsupported statuses, unresolved references, missing required measures, duplicate run identities, or a decision inconsistent with the sealed transition table.
- **Fixture:** Exercise the table with blocked, invalid, valid-no-go, valid-go-with-missing-proof, and valid-go-all-pass cases.
- **Live evidence check:** Resolve representative and mandatory references through the selected durable scope chains and root rollups, host/fault records, owning tests, and composed scenario.
- **Manual review:** Trace every narrative answer to the fixed tables, verify all 35 §43 rows and every §44 category, confirm AC9-only scope, and scan for post-hoc changes, secret leakage, significance/confidence language, unsupported causality, or an exactly-once claim.

## Design Gate
Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §0, §43, §32, §33, §44; decomposed from epic ravel-4dw via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e10-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.
