title: Run the fixed multi-host Change proof
description:
## Context

E09 is a proof epic. Focused unit and composition tests establish protocol behavior, but the acceptance criteria also require the concrete fixed migration to run across several real hosts and reach its configured autonomous stopping condition through the actual candidate, evaluator, model, Git, and code-host paths.

This run proves only E09 composition. Comparative treatments and a reusable experiment harness belong to E10 or the prerequisite epics. One exception: if this run consumes the reserved E01 treatment-C observation slot (ravel-j4t), it must execute exactly the frozen E01 C fault profile and capture contract instead of the default no-fault composition profile; otherwise it is proof-only and E10 runs the C observation separately.

## Current State

The repository currently contains design documents and beads metadata but no code. `docs/epics.md` E09 defines the live proof requirements, and `docs/mvp-outline.md` §18 describes several hosts working against one campaign base and final rediscovery. E01 (`ravel-q3w`) supplies the precommitted safe repository, campaign branch policy, several-dozen-target migration, fixed treatment, evaluator set, providers/fixed model configurations, budgets, depth-two cap, and stopping criteria.

This task requires Steps 1–6 and the completed E06–E08 live paths. Existing prerequisite tests already own worker loss/reclaim, scoped-controller failover, stale-fence rejection, evaluator fault matrices, and full publisher recovery matrices.

## Desired State

The fixed E01 Change migration runs on at least three independent machine/VM hosts. Several hosts construct candidates concurrently against the declared source base OID. The root scoped controller autonomously gates observations and semantic judgment, admits at most one fresh retry plan, serializes accepted work through one campaign branch/PR, reconciles one ambiguous publisher outcome, closes every target ledger entry, performs final trusted rediscovery, and reaches the configured success or explicit-unresolved stopping condition without routine human intervention.

Retained artifacts make the proof auditable: exact campaign/scope/parent/delegation/plan/work-revision/claim-fence/scope-epoch/grant identities, scope histories and root rollups, host/claim participation, source base OID, target/group records, attempt and candidate identities, exact deterministic observations, scoped decisions, child certificates/settlements where used, escrow/unknown-reserve accounting, integration observations, ambiguous-operation reconciliation, terminal target counts/reasons, final discovery revision/result, and stop reason.

## Implementation Guidance

Use the one node binary and concrete `src/workflows/change/` path. Run against the E01-selected safe repository and campaign branch. Use actual E06 models, E07 candidate construction, E08 trusted evaluators/code-host publisher, and the durable scope histories and root rollups.

Exercise only these E09 composition edges under root-depth-one/direct-child-depth-two limits: concurrent hosts, complete evidence before judgment, mechanical failure precedence, one admitted fresh retry plan, deterministic serial integration, one ambiguous publisher operation, complete target accounting, final rediscovery, and autonomous stop. Do not add worker-loss/reclaim replay, scoped-controller failover, a generic fault runner, treatment comparison, metrics service, dashboard, baseline framework, or experiment framework — unless the run consumes the reserved E01 treatment-C slot, in which case execute exactly the frozen E01 C fault profile and capture contract (still no generic fault runner or experiment framework).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] At least three independent hosts participate, and multiple hosts construct distinct candidates concurrently against the identical declared source base OID.
- [ ] The run uses the fixed E01 treatment, grouping/cap, repository, branch, evaluator set, fixed model configurations, budgets, depth-two limit, and stop condition without post-hoc changes.
- [ ] No semantic judgment starts before the complete required deterministic evidence set passes, and an exercised mechanical failure cannot be overridden by semantic approval.
- [ ] One exercised rejection supplies typed basis for exactly one admitted fresh retry `WorkSpec` with new attempt/candidate identities; no target exceeds two ordinary attempts.
- [ ] Accepted work is applied serially through one campaign branch and one campaign PR: the PR remains open while candidates accumulate, each applied candidate reaches `APPLIED_TO_CAMPAIGN_BRANCH_AND_CHECKED`, and exactly one campaign-level merge request follows established completeness.
- [ ] One ambiguous publisher outcome is reconciled from code-host state before retry or release of the serial slot, with no duplicate authoritative integration.
- [ ] Every discovered target has exactly one `RESOLVED`, `REJECTED`, `BLOCKED`, or `UNRESOLVED` outcome with retained reason/provenance.
- [ ] Final trusted discovery runs over the exact final campaign-branch head and leaves no unclassified legacy target.
- [ ] The configured autonomous stop is reached without humans assigning targets, choosing ordinary candidates, approving routine semantic decisions, or approving routine safe-branch integration.
- [ ] Retained scope decisions/observations/artifacts, child certificates/settlements, and accounting records are sufficient to trace every assertion above to exact identities and revisions.
- [ ] If this run consumes the reserved E01 treatment-C slot, it executes the frozen E01 C fault profile and capture contract and records the reserved C run ID and required measurement records; otherwise it is proof-only.
- [ ] Manual diff review finds a concrete `workflows::change` module and only demonstrated shared helpers, with no workflow trait/DSL, campaign profile, generic discovery interface, planner, custom merge queue, backend framework, or E10-owned experiment machinery.

## Testing Strategy

Run this as a live integration proof on at least three independent hosts. Before the run, perform the E01 preflight and record immutable configuration/source identities. During the run, inject or select one deterministic mechanical failure, one first-candidate semantic rejection, and one ambiguous publisher result using existing controls. After stop, use a fixed proof-check script or queries over retained records to verify host concurrency, identity axis, scope depth, the two-attempt maximum, certificate/settlement closure, serial integration, reconciliation, terminal accounting, and final discovery. Finish with manual artifact and implementation-diff review. Do not repeat worker-loss/reclaim or prerequisite fault suites.

## Design Gate

Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §18, §16; decomposed from epic ravel-e1n via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e09-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

## Final Step

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.

## Description

Run the two frozen precommitted three-treatment comparisons and issue one go/no-go
report. Reuse the
correctness, failure, distributed, and recursive proof artifacts produced by the
owning epics rather than recreating a cross-cutting recovery framework. Add one final
end-to-end multi-machine kill-and-recovery scenario showing that scoped heads, claims,
grants, observations, certificates, and settlement compose.

Analysis is offline and descriptive. Existing frozen Research and Change experiment
contracts, scoped campaign decisions, provider usage records, immutable traces,
evaluator results, and code-host records supply the measurements; the experiment must
not create a telemetry product or change its success definition after observing
results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Research and Change each run the frozen single-agent, single-machine multi-agent, and distributed multi-machine treatments under the precommitted inputs, bounds, run counts, schedules, and success definitions.
- [ ] The distributed treatment uses at least three independent machines/VM hosts and includes a late join, active-worker loss, scoped-controller failover, remote model/judge/evaluator work, fresh scope-selective SQLite reconstruction, child certification where used, and settlement.
- [ ] One final end-to-end scenario kills an active worker and parent or child controller around an external unknown outcome, then demonstrates exact `ScopeHead` and scope-chain recovery, separate `scope_epoch` and `claim_fence` rejection, grant and operation reconciliation, certificate handling, idempotent settlement, conserved escrow, bounded recovery, and coherent completion or explicit unresolved state.
- [ ] Research reports wall time, supported/incorrect/omitted conclusions, useful evidence, discriminating follow-up, provider usage/cost, duplicate work, scope/grant overhead, settlement, quarantined unknown reserve, and scaling efficiency.
- [ ] Change reports resolved targets, omissions, semantic correction/rejection, conflicts, wasted work, usage/cost per target, utilization, scope/grant overhead, settlement, quarantined unknown reserve, scaling efficiency, and final rediscovery.
- [ ] Autonomous proof shows that humans supplied only objective/configuration or explicitly configured proposal observations and did not assign work, approve routine conclusions, choose ordinary candidates, mint grants, override admission, or perform routine safe-branch integration.
- [ ] Correctness evidence references the owning epic tests for frozen-v1 S3 ambiguity, SQLite atomic projection, and claim fencing and for scoped-v2 mixed-version rejection, selective replay, scope authority, admission, grants, escrow, provider unknown outcomes, process cleanup, trusted evaluation, code-host reconciliation, certificates, and settlement.
- [ ] One small offline renderer emits CSV and Markdown with two fixed tables: Research and Change. No metrics service, dashboard, exporter framework, permanent baseline mode, adaptive reruns, or significance claim is added.
- [ ] The report gives a go/no-go recommendation and answers where distribution helped, where it stopped scaling, whether judge diversity and disagreement added value, what work was duplicated, and whether S3, scoped-controller, admission, settlement, or evaluator paths were bottlenecks.
- [ ] MVP completion is denied unless the section 43 invariants, recursive architecture gates, escrow equation, verifier-bounded completion, and actual multi-machine/failover requirements are demonstrated; a no-go result remains a valid completed feasibility experiment.

value: E03 design decision (ravel-1l4.2, judged + rust-code-reviewer/ponytail sign-off): v1 stays frozen at 3 content kinds. Converter in src/sync/event.rs maps CampaignCreated@1 / WorkflowStarted@seq>1 to SchedulingEffect rows whose id = 16-digit zero-padded sequence (projected_id); ArtifactPublished -> ConversionError::UnsupportedContent (fail closed); wrong position -> IllegalPosition. No work/objective/dependency variants until E06 (ravel-85q.3) introduces payload-bearing work-creation events and real ids. work_items/objectives/dependencies stay empty all of E03; 1l4.6 seeds its predicate fixture rows directly and owns the columns its predicate reads. Sequence-derived ids unique only within one ancestry: divergence detection in 1l4.5 must compare digests, never sequence alone. No _ wildcard on EventContent match — future variant must break the build.

ravel-1l4.6 resolved contracts (task-owner decisions on spec OPEN QUESTIONS): (1) refresh is handle-level: pub async refresh(store, &DbHandle) -> Readiness; startup signature unchanged; local validation failures surface at startup (no handle => no refresh), so refresh-level NotReady covers only its own replay attempt. (2) Readiness = Ready{local_cursor, observed_head: full Head} | NotReady(reason); reasons mirror ReplayError variants plus Behind/Ahead/TailMismatch comparator outcomes; a failed refresh's return value IS the state (nothing cached). (3) NO new WireError variant: unknown version stays WireError::InvalidValue per E02's frozen error taxonomy; digest failures are ReferenceMismatch, so version-vs-digest stays distinguishable; do not touch E02 wire code in .6 (spec step 3 deviation, recorded). (4) Work vocabulary: work_items.state TEXT CHECK IN ('ready','done','cancelled'), schedulable='ready', satisfied-terminal='done'; budget_remaining INTEGER CHECK >= 0, admission = > 0. campaigns.state/workflows.state TEXT CHECK IN ('active','completed'), apply inserts 'active'. (5) capabilities: exact strings, stored as space-joined sorted unique tokens in work_items.required_capabilities TEXT NOT NULL ('' = none); no Capability domain type. (6) NO workflows.campaign_id column: one database projects one chain/campaign (singleton cursor invariant); work_items.workflow_id added for grouping/order. (7) list_ready_work returns owned (workflow_id, work_id) pairs; limit clamped privately at 1024; after rotation via std rotate after ordered query. Schema v2 (SCHEMA_VERSION 1->2), old files rebuild via existing mechanism.

e06-admitted-work-witness (ravel-yno DQ1, 3-judge panel unanimous for Option A, overturning the plan's Option B recommendation): AC1 'WorkRef values can be constructed only from admitted work rows' binds WorkRef itself, not a second witness type. Seal it: WorkRef::new becomes pub(crate) and KEEPS a mechanism-honest name (pub(crate) fn new or from_parts) because ~20 in-crate test sites fabricate references through the same constructor -- a name like from_admitted_row would overstate what the compiler checks; the production invariant (mintable only from an admitted_work row or the admission insert that writes one; wire decoding cannot produce one) lives in the doc comment. GrantActivatedPayload holds WorkId + a revision integer instead of a WorkRef, keeping the existing zero/MAX_STORED_INTEGER range check, so grant_activated_from_decoded cannot mint one from untrusted bytes; the durable FOLD_GRANT_SQL rowcount-0 Conflict stays the authority that refuses unadmitted work. WireGrantActivatedPayload is untouched and no fixture bytes change. decode_grant and decode_bound keep taking expected_work: &WorkRef from their row-reading caller and must not construct one. Do NOT add an AdmittedWork type and do NOT add a second ScopeClaimIdentity constructor; its existing new stays. Do NOT add a #[cfg(test)] constructor -- it would be a second mint path and is invisible to tests/ anyway. tests/wire.rs: relocate scope_keys_cover_the_exact_identity_axis into the in-crate mod tests in src/scope.rs with its expected key strings verbatim, then narrow scope_claim_key/scope_grant_key to pub(crate). Accepted weakness: inside one crate pub(crate) is convention plus doc, not compiler enforcement; the panel judged literal AC fidelity plus closing the wire mint site worth more than the type-level row-vs-bytes distinction Option B preserved.

e06-bedrock-invocation-operation (ravel-85q.1, 3-judge fork panel, Option B = Converse by majority; AMENDS the 'non-streaming InvokeModel only' clause of e06-provider-transport-dependency on NEW EVIDENCE that neither the original panel nor the rust sign-off had -- both reasoned only about streaming vs non-streaming, and Converse is equally non-streaming, its streaming sibling being ConverseStream). Use non-streaming Converse ONLY: not ConverseStream, not InvokeModel, not InvokeModelWithResponseStream. The original panel's stated reason (avoid the eventstream surface and partial-response outcomes) is preserved exactly. Why: the token cap is one typed field, InferenceConfiguration.max_tokens, instead of a per-family JSON key the adapter owns with nothing checking it landed (Anthropic max_tokens vs Nova inferenceConfig.max_new_tokens vs Titan textGenerationConfig.maxTokenCount); reported use is typed TokenUsage instead of a hand-written parse of an unversioned model dialect, and that parse would need its own malformed-response outcome firing on an HTTP 200 the account was already billed for, which is exactly the ambiguous state ravel-85q.4 exists to reconcile; AC1's small typed outcome set falls out of the non-optional stop_reason whose variants already name refusal (ContentFiltered, GuardrailIntervened), cap-hit (MaxTokens, ModelContextWindowExceeded) and malformed (MalformedModelOutput). The digest objection does not survive: digesting SDK wire bytes would make operation identity sensitive to smithy serialization changes across SDK upgrades, so the same logical request would digest differently after a bump. Binding: token cap set from the model profile on every request via InferenceConfiguration::max_tokens, and the adapter composes NO request JSON body and owns NO per-model dialect. Reported use comes from ConverseOutput::usage -> TokenUsage input_tokens/output_tokens/total_tokens copied out as scalars; CAREFUL, usage is Option<TokenUsage> even though the counts inside it are non-optional i32, so usage == None on a success response is a distinct terminal condition recorded as reported-use-unavailable, never as zero and never as 'the call did not happen' (ravel-85q.4 treats it as a completed invocation with unknown usage, not an unknown outcome). One judge wrongly asserted the SDK guarantees usage is present or the call failed; that is false and must not be implemented. The request digest covers the adapter's own canonical serialization of its owned request type (model id, model-configuration id, the InferenceConfiguration fields, system blocks, messages), NOT SDK wire bytes and NEVER Debug output; state at the digest site that it identifies an invocation rather than reproducing the wire frame, so ravel-85q.2's manifests keep a definition that survives SDK upgrades. Outcome mapping comes from stop_reason plus the typed error variants with no string matching on a model dialect; the bare-429-lands-in-Unhandled gap applies to both operations and the fake transport must cover it. ACCEPTED COST, verified in 1.139.0: InvokeModelInput/Output redact body wholesale in Debug so InvokeModel would get payload-logging hygiene free, whereas ConverseInput's Debug redacts only prompt_variables and request_metadata, ContentBlock's hand-written Debug redacts only ReasoningContent and prints Text(val) in full, and SystemContentBlock plus both ConverseOutput types derive Debug with no redaction -- so the adapter MUST NOT Debug-print or log any ConverseInput, ConverseOutput (either operation output or types::ConverseOutput), Message, ContentBlock or SystemContentBlock, and must convert to owned domain types at the boundary and log only those. Also do not put Message, ContentBlock, TokenUsage or StopReason into durable records, and do not use tool_config, guardrail_config or additional_model_request_fields in this MVP. Practical note: types::ConverseOutput and operation::converse::ConverseOutput collide by name, so alias on import.

e06-bedrock-sdk-facts (verified against the vendored aws-sdk-bedrockruntime 1.139.0 source in ~/.cargo/registry, for ravel-85q.1): the crate exposes operations apply_guardrail, converse, converse_stream, count_tokens, get_async_invoke, invoke_guardrail_checks, invoke_model, invoke_model_with_bidirectional_stream, invoke_model_with_response_stream, list_async_invokes, start_async_invoke. DECISIVE FINDING: InvokeModelInput has NO typed max-tokens field -- its fields are body (an opaque aws_smithy_types::Blob of model-specific JSON), content_type, accept, model_id, trace, guardrail_identifier, guardrail_version, performance_config_latency, service_tier, request_metadata -- so with InvokeModel the token cap must be hand-composed into a per-model JSON dialect and the reported usage must be parsed back out of one. ConverseInput instead carries model_id, messages, system, inference_config, tool_config, guardrail_config, additional_model_request_fields, prompt_variables, request_metadata, performance_config, service_tier, output_config, where types::InferenceConfiguration has a TYPED max_tokens: Option<i32> alongside temperature, top_p, stop_sequences. ConverseOutput carries output, a non-optional stop_reason: types::StopReason, usage: Option<types::TokenUsage>, metrics, additional_model_response_fields, trace, performance_config, service_tier. types::TokenUsage has non-optional input_tokens/output_tokens/total_tokens: i32 plus optional cache_read_input_tokens, cache_write_input_tokens, cache_details. StopReason variants: ContentFiltered, EndTurn, GuardrailIntervened, MalformedModelOutput, MalformedToolUse, MaxTokens, ModelContextWindowExceeded, StopSequence, ToolUse. ConverseError variants (from src/error_meta.rs): AccessDeniedException, InternalServerException, ModelErrorException, ModelNotReadyException, ModelTimeoutException, ResourceNotFoundException, ServiceUnavailableException, ThrottlingException, ValidationException, Unhandled -- so throttling is a TYPED variant needing no string matching. Consequence: Converse satisfies AC1 (typed request and outcome), AC2 (token cap as a typed field), AC4 (typed usage decodes to owned domain types with no JSON-dialect parsing) and mvp-outline section 13's required reported token use, while InvokeModel satisfies none of them without hand-parsing a model-specific dialect; and AC5's six cases each map to a typed match (success EndTurn, refusal ContentFiltered/GuardrailIntervened, rate limit ThrottlingException, timeout ModelTimeoutException plus the SDK timeout error, transport failure SdkError::DispatchFailure, malformed response MalformedModelOutput plus SdkError::ResponseError).

e06-converse-usage-is-not-optional-on-the-wire (verified by test against aws-sdk-bedrockruntime 1.139.0, CORRECTS e06-bedrock-invocation-operation): the ruling said ConverseOutput::usage == None is a distinct terminal condition ('reported-use-unavailable', a completed invocation with unknown usage). That condition IS NOT REACHABLE FROM THE WIRE. usage is a required member of the Converse output shape, so a frame that omits the key entirely still deserializes to Some(TokenUsage { input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0, total_tokens: 0 }), and an explicit "usage":null does the same. Measured both ways. CONSEQUENCE FOR ravel-85q.2 AND ravel-85q.4: zero counts are NOT evidence that no tokens were billed, because an omitted or null usage block is indistinguishable from a genuine zero report. A manifest or trace must not treat zeros as proof of zero spend, and reconciliation must not infer 'the call did not happen' from them. The Option<ReportedUse> arm is retained in InvocationOutcome::Completed as a defensive total case with a doc comment saying the deserializer does not currently produce it, following the same precedent as is_cyclic in src/domain/proposal.rs (a branch kept because the rule has to be total, not because an input reaches it). The test an_omitted_usage_block_reports_zeros_rather_than_absence pins the reachable behavior rather than the unreachable one.

e06-observation-attribution (ravel-yno DQ2, 3-judge panel, Option A by majority): AC3 'Observations and actions retain the proposal basis and effect-grant attribution used to produce them' is DEFERRED as a record and LANDED as a contract, because no observation or action payload type exists anywhere in the codebase and mvp-outline explicitly forbids inventing the terminal-decision representation before that contract is resolved. Rationale: AC3 is already structurally satisfied for anything bound to an admitted revision -- admitted_work.plan_digest names the content-addressed PlanProposal whose own bases field records the typed proposal basis, and applied_scope_events.grant_digest names the authorizing EffectGrant. No schema change, no SCHEMA_VERSION bump, no forced projection rebuild, and no new payload type in ravel-yno; minting one here would fork the canonical scoped-v2 artifact-reference payload that ravel-85q.2 is chartered to define first (see e06-artifact-ref-event when it lands). Binding contract for whoever lands the first observation/action payload type: it MUST bind the admitted revision (scope, plan digest, work revision), the claim fence, the attempt, and the authorizing EffectGrant digest. ravel-yno pins today's mechanism with a test that the CHECK ((payload_type = 'grant_activated') = (grant_digest IS NOT NULL)) biconditional refuses BOTH directions -- a grant_activated row without a grant digest and a grant digest under any other payload type. The PR must state AC3 is partially met and name ravel-85q.2 as the completing task.

e06-provider-transport-dependency (ravel-85q.1 DQ1, 3-judge panel, Option A by majority): ADD aws-sdk-bedrockruntime as a pinned direct dependency and build the transport on it; do NOT hand-roll SigV4 and do NOT ship a provider-less stub. Cargo.toml [dependencies] mirrors the aws-sdk-s3 block exactly: default-features = false, features [default-https-client, rt-tokio], exact = version pin RESOLVED at implementation time (do not invent one; one judge guessed a 1.135-era version, which is not a fact). [dev-dependencies] adds the same crate with default-features = false, features [test-util]. Rationale: the S3 SDK already puts aws-runtime, aws-sigv4, aws-types, aws-credential-types and the aws-smithy-* stack in Cargo.lock, so Bedrock Runtime (REST-JSON) adds one direct crate and little transitive tree; Option B was not even dependency-free, because aws-sigv4 1.5.1 is present in the lock but is NOT a declared direct dependency, so using it would also require a new direct dep while additionally putting request canonicalization and auth on hand-written code; Option C cannot answer AC2 or AC3 (AC3 literally names SDK retries, so with no SDK there are nothing to disable) and would leave ravel-85q.2 manifests/traces and ravel-85q.4 unknown outcomes binding to provider request id and reported token use that nothing produces, per mvp-outline section 13's required immutable metadata. PIN GATE, corrected against the verified baseline: the lock ALREADY carries duplicate majors for aws-smithy-eventstream (0.60.21, 0.61.1), aws-smithy-http (0.63.6, 0.64.0), aws-smithy-json (0.62.7, 0.63.0), aws-smithy-observability (0.2.6, 0.3.0), aws-smithy-schema (0.1.0, 0.2.0) and aws-smithy-xml (0.60.15, 0.62.0), so the gate is that the chosen pin adds NO NEW duplicate major beyond that baseline, not that none exists. Binding implementation constraints: non-streaming InvokeModel only (no InvokeModelWithResponseStream, which drags in the eventstream surface and a partial-response outcome the typed set does not model); client construction copies configured() at src/storage/s3.rs:446 applying RetryConfig::disabled(), TimeoutConfig operation+attempt timeouts, StalledStreamProtectionConfig::enabled() and behavior_version_latest() AFTER the caller's builder so supplied config cannot re-enable retries; NO tokio::time in the adapter -- bounds come from TimeoutConfig, which keeps the adapter clear of the implicit tokio/time feature unification that src/distributed/grants.rs already relies on; AttemptHistory marked BEFORE the await, with only a pre-dispatch rejection and a ConstructionFailure on clean history proving no send while transport, timeout, malformed response and unclassified service errors stay possible-send; nothing from aws_sdk_bedrockruntime crosses into a durable record (decode to owned domain types at the boundary, no SDK error type, no Blob, no credential material stored or logged) and the request digest covers the canonical request bytes the adapter builds, never an SDK struct's Debug; tests drive the real SDK through aws-smithy-runtime test-util StaticReplayClient and NeverClient as the S3 tests do, and AC3 gets a checkable test rather than an assertion -- a replay client returning one retryable 429 must record exactly one request and yield the rate-limit outcome.

e06-provider-transport-dependency-pin-evidence (empirical result of the PIN GATE that e06-provider-transport-dependency required, measured in ravel-wt/85q.1): aws-sdk-bedrockruntime =1.139.0 is the pin. Adding it resolves onto the existing tree with ZERO change to the aws/smithy crate set -- diff of the locked aws-credential-types / aws-runtime / aws-types / aws-smithy-* name+version set before and after is empty, and the duplicate-major list is unchanged (aws-smithy-eventstream, aws-smithy-http, aws-smithy-json, aws-smithy-observability, aws-smithy-schema, aws-smithy-xml were already duplicated in the baseline and remain exactly as they were). Cargo.lock grew by one crate only, 262 to 263 entries, 31 inserted lines, and the sole added name is aws-sdk-bedrockruntime itself: no transitive additions at all. cargo check builds clean with it. This closes the caveat both judges flagged as the one thing that would have made Option C preferable ('if the resolved Bedrock Runtime pin drags in a different smithy major, the near-zero cost claim collapses'). Note cargo check --locked FAILS when first adding the dependency because the lock must be regenerated; run plain cargo check once to update the lock, then --locked holds for every later run.

e06-transport-signoff-conditions (rust-code-reviewer sign-off on ravel-85q.1's two rulings: SIGN OFF WITH CONDITIONS on both; no hard blockers, both defects are wording not design). Conditions accepted, independent of the pending Converse-vs-InvokeModel fork: (1) THE 429 TEST AS SPECIFIED PROVES THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT IT CLAIMS. Variant resolution goes through generic.code() (src/protocol_serde/shape_invoke_model.rs:13), so a replay response carrying only status 429 deserializes to Unhandled, NOT ThrottlingException. The replay response must carry 429 PLUS the x-amzn-errortype: ThrottlingException header (or a JSON body with __type/code). (2) The sibling retryable variants ServiceQuotaExceededException, ServiceUnavailableException and ModelNotReadyException must be classified deliberately rather than falling into a wildcard arm; ModelNotReadyException is documented as SDK-auto-retried up to 5 times, which RetryConfig::disabled() switches off, so the adapter owns that decision now. (3) The tokio/time rationale in e06-provider-transport-dependency is WRONG and is corrected here: rt-tokio enables tokio/time transitively (aws-smithy-async declares rt-tokio = ["tokio/time"]) exactly as aws-sdk-s3 already does, so the unification is pre-existing and unavoidable; the binding rule is 'the adapter contains no tokio::time calls', not 'keeps the adapter clear of the feature unification'. (4) The no-Debug-digest rule has a stronger mechanism than leakage: InvokeModelInput and InvokeModelOutput Debug print '*** Sensitive Data Redacted ***' for body, so a digest taken over Debug would be CONSTANT ACROSS DISTINCT PROMPTS. Cite that mechanism in the code comment. (5) 'Within the model profile's permitted range' has no referent -- grep finds no model-profile type in src/, the only hit being docs/epics.md:27 listing 'fixed model profiles' as a planning item. Pre-dispatch cap validation needs a concrete range source or the criterion is uncheckable; smallest workable thing is a const table in the transport module keyed by model id. (6) The prohibition should grep the bare Rust identifiers reserved_budget_units (on Proposal at src/domain/proposal.rs:246,299,574) and limit_units, not the SQL column name scopes.reserved_budget_units. Also confirmed: every config knob S3 uses exists on aws_sdk_bedrockruntime::config::Builder under the same names (retry_config, timeout_config, stalled_stream_protection, behavior_version_latest, region, credentials_provider, endpoint_url, http_client), StalledStreamProtectionConfig and Credentials are re-exported from that config module, and default-https-client / rt-tokio / test-util are all real features of 1.139.0 with test-util supplying Credentials::for_tests() plus StaticReplayClient and NeverClient. The lock claim holds; aws-smithy-json 0.63.0 merely moves from dev-only into the normal graph, which is cosmetic. There is no unused_crate_dependencies lint, so the dependency sits unused without failing clippy.

e06-transport-token-cap (ravel-85q.1 DQ2, 3-judge panel unanimous for Option A): the token cap is a per-request transport parameter ONLY; the transport integrates with no budget substrate. AC2's word is 'explicit', not 'enforced', and it sits in a list with provider, model profile, request digest, timeout and retry policy -- all properties of one request, not of a campaign. reserved_budget_units and limit_units are opaque integer counters with no token semantics anywhere in the codebase, so reading them as token budgets would assign a meaning nothing else supports AND would silently pre-decide the substrate question ravel-85q.4 explicitly owns and has not settled. Binding: the cap is a required typed non-Option field on the request (max_output_tokens: NonZeroU32 style -- no default, no builder path that can omit it, no 0 sentinel); the adapter sends it as the model configuration's max-tokens value and includes it in the bytes the request digest covers, so two calls differing only in cap get different digests and therefore different operation identity; pre-dispatch validation is the transport's only enforcement (cap present and within the model profile's permitted range, rejected before send with a proven-not-sent outcome) and that branch carries the runnable check; reported token use from the response is recorded as REPORTED, never as confirmed spend, per mvp-outline section 13 ('Reported usage is not confirmed spend until authoritative reconciliation'); the transport module contains ZERO references to scopes.reserved_budget_units and to grant limit_units; the typed request and outcome must expose the cap and the reported use so ravel-85q.4 can wrap the transport with pre-send campaign checks without growing the adapter's signature, which is what keeps 85q.4 from becoming an N+1-parameter change. Accepted weakness the panel named: a cap the transport only forwards prevents no overspend, since a caller looping with valid per-call caps burns any budget; under this reading AC2 buys metadata fidelity and operation identity, not safety, and real protection arrives only with ravel-85q.4.
